papers.title: Emerging Strategies for Bioprinting Organized Musculoskeletal Tissues with Biomimetic Collagen Architecture.
papers.abstract: Collagen fiber organization is critical to the biomechanical function of musculoskeletal tissues. This has motivated increased interest in tissue engineering strategies aiming to recapitulate native collagen architecture in order to generate more biomimetic grafts. In particular, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting has emerged as a powerful biofabrication platform capable of generating patient-specific constructs containing cells, supporting biomaterials, and diverse regulatory factors (e.g., genes, proteins, and small molecules). This paper will review how emerging bioprinting strategies can also be used to provide spatially defined external and/or internal biophysical cues to cells, thereby modulating their phenotype and the organization of the extracellular matrix they produce in culture. Furthermore, we will explore how postbioprinting interventions such as temporal enzymatic treatments and mechanical stimulation can be used to further promote cell and collagen alignment, matrix remodeling, and tissue maturation. Together, these approaches hold significant promise for the development of next-generation grafts for the treatment of diverse musculoskeletal injuries.

papers.title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are gaining attention in autonomous driving, inheriting commonsense priors from large language models (LLMs) and widening the navigation interface from a fixed command set to free-form natural-language instructions. However, this open-ended interface exposes a new vulnerability surface: an inattentive driver may issue instructions that are unsafe given the current scene, and a malicious user may issue dangerous ones on purpose. We present the first benchmark suite that evaluates navigation following and conflict awareness together, along with adversarial robustness. Existing VLAs fall short on both: SimLingo completes no language-instructed lane change in closed loop, and all models degrade sharply under conflicting signals. We propose SafeDriveVLA, the first driving VLA that (1) explicitly predicts a three-level navigation-compliance mode to decouple conflict reasoning from action generation, and (2) uses navigation-conditioned world model dreaming to inform this prediction. Unlike prior world models that roll out expert or planned actions, ours dreams of strictly following the navigation signal, showing when following is safe. SafeDriveVLA reaches 88.16 Driving Score (DS) and 68.64% Success Rate (SR) on Bench2Drive, lifts closed-loop language following by 49.3% and reduces collisions under unsafe instructions from 60 to 38 compared to the best SimLingo variant. Video demonstrations are available on our project page.

papers.title: HRTF Upsampling and Personalization via Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Head-related transfer function (HRTF) spatial upsampling from sparse measurements is a fundamental challenge in personalized binaural audio. We formulate HRTF upsampling as an operator learning problem and introduce SPARO, a neural operator that maps sparse measurements at a set of spatial directions to the HRTF field, a continuous representation that can be queried at arbitrary positions. SPARO projects the measurements onto a learned set of spherical latent modes, processes the latent modes with Transformer blocks, and decodes the resulting representations at query directions. On SONICOM, using the LAP24 measurement configuration, SPARO attains the best log-spectral distortion (LSD) and interaural level difference (ILD) error at every sparsity level from 3 to 100 measurements (18% lower LSD and 43% lower ILD error than the strongest baseline at 100 measurements) while remaining competitive in interaural time difference (ITD) error. It reconstructs a dense HRTF 15 to 373 times faster than the leading neural-field method RANF. We further validate the approach on HUTUBS, demonstrating its effectiveness across HRTF datasets.

papers.title: From Human Corrections to Learned Segmentations: A Critical Mathematical Review of Information, Learning, and Human Effort
papers.abstract: When does a human correction become useful learning, and what establishes better segmentation at matched human effort? This critical narrative review follows feedback through its selection, learner update, and evaluation. It compares active learning, machine teaching, interactive segmentation, and sequential predictive evaluation using a common mathematical account of target information, predictive error, response predictability, and human work. An exact Bayesian update converts evaluation-label information into expected log-loss improvement; an excess-risk decomposition explains what an approximate learner can lose. Conditional information decompositions separate the roles of selected locations, labels, and displayed context. Empirical comparisons show why response protocols, update mechanisms, and effort denominators matter, distinguishing current-mask refinement from reusable learning and simulated interaction from human evidence. We identify what logs can reveal, what requires independent evaluation, and what remains model-dependent. The resulting research priorities are to test what selection reveals, whether using it improves assimilation, and whether the resulting interaction policy benefits segmentation at matched effort. These are distinct claims: predicting a teacher's responses need not identify human intentions or establish better learning. No new acquisition algorithm or empirical superiority is claimed.

papers.title: Look Before You Restore: Learning to Predict Before Acting for Agentic Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Agents for mixed-degradation image restoration typically learn what a tool does to an image only after running it: failed calls waste computation and harmful outputs go unnoticed until too late. We propose PreActIR, an agentic restoration framework that predicts tool consequences before execution. For each candidate tool, a tool-conditioned world model forecasts changes in residual degradation, image quality, and fidelity, together with the risk of harm and the uncertainty of the prediction. The agent executes the top-ranked candidate, and an independent verifier commits or rolls back its output before the agent replans from the observed state. PreActIR also audits whether performance is limited by the selector or by the candidate space, and studies targeted tool adaptation as a controlled way to expand that space. In a controlled evaluation that fixes the candidate pool, verifier, and budget and employs reference-annotated degradation states, PreActIR uses 42.5% fewer real tool calls and 63.4% fewer rejected calls than reactive, execute-then-evaluate trial and error, while improving Y-PSNR by 0.92 dB.

papers.title: Fractional is Better: Learnable Derivative Orders in Neural Operator Learning
papers.abstract: Neural operators learn mappings between function spaces, enabling fast surrogate solutions to partial differential equations. Despite remarkable architectural diversity, these methods often share a common input representation: raw coordinate-value pairs $(x, u(x))$. We ask whether inputs aligned with PDE differential structure can improve learning. Through Picard iteration on mild solutions, we show that derivatives of the input appear explicitly in the solution operator, suggesting that providing derivative features should reduce the network's implicit differentiation burden. We prove this intuition: providing derivative features improves approximation bounds from $O(W^{-(s-m)/d})$ to $O(W^{-s/d})$, where $W$ is parameter count, $s$ is input regularity, $m$ is the PDE order, and $d$ is spatial dimension. Our central finding, however, is a surprise: the optimal derivative order $β^*$ is strictly less than the PDE order $m$. This gap arises from a bias-variance tradeoff in spectral space that we characterize in closed form. Learning $β$ from data achieves automatic spectral regularization. We introduce $\partial$-NO (del-NO), for derivative-augmented neural operators, an architecture-agnostic augmentation that provides learnable fractional derivative features to any neural operator backbone. Across benchmark problems and architectures, $\partial$-NO consistently improves prediction accuracy, with learned orders that reflect a representation of known physics modulated by noise and finite-sample constraints.

papers.title: Hierarchical Gaussian Processes for Survey Weighting: Local Equivalent Weights in Structured Populations
papers.abstract: Regression-based survey weighting connects model-based population estimation with design-based inference through equivalent weights. For nonlinear models, equivalent weights can be defined locally through the sensitivity of a poststratified population estimator. However, conventional regression models may inadequately capture nonlinear relationships and complex interactions across sparse poststratification cells. We develop a survey-weighting framework based on hierarchical Gaussian process (HGP) regression, combining structured group-level effects with kernel-based smoothing to share information across related cells. We derive Gaussian posterior prediction formulas that exploit the structured covariance representation to reduce computational costs. We also establish a uniform convergence result for the posterior predictive mean under stated regularity conditions and construct local equivalent weights by matching the first-order sensitivity of a plug-in poststratified estimand to that of a weighted average of fitted response means, with both derivatives taken with respect to the latent mean-scale vector. Simulations show that HGP achieves lower population-weighted prediction error under nonparametric structure, whereas logistic regression performs well under correct parametric specification. Additional analyses examine sample size, frame coverage, subgroup prediction, and population-mean agreement. An application to the Future of Families and Child Wellbeing Study illustrates the method. Overall, this work extends local equivalent-weight construction to nonparametric modeling and provides a computational framework and conditional theoretical results for survey weighting in structured, sparse populations.

papers.title: Learning-Based Adaptive MPC for Magnetorquer-Only Satellite Attitude Control
papers.abstract: Nanosatellites (e.g., CubeSats) have the potential to carry out useful science and exploration activities for outer solar system exploration, but their small size leads to tradeoffs between attitude control and science capabilities. Magnetorquers offer a unique compromise as compact actuators that enable three-axis attitude control, but suffer from a loss of control authority and require full knowledge of the planetary magnetic field. In this work, we present a learning-based adaptive model predictive control (MPC) algorithm that plans rotational trajectories for the satellite while accounting for this loss of control authority. Key to our approach is the inclusion of a learned magnetic field model that is trained in simulation using low-fidelity magnetic field data. Using measurements collected online, our proposed algorithm adapts this learned magnetic field model using a simple last-layer update scheme, allowing the MPC controller to quickly adapt to the true planetary magnetic field model and more effectively plan attitude trajectories. We demonstrate the results of our proposed approach for two use cases, (1) Earth-orbit and (2) Uranus-orbit, and show that our learning-based adaptive MPC algorithm improves controller success for these system simulations by 5% and 61%, respectively.

papers.title: PAWA: Panoramic Action-conditioned World Modeling for Multiple Agents
papers.abstract: A multiplayer world model must predict how the independent actions of several players change a shared environment, including changes outside a player's current field of view. A point-of-view (POV) video captures such changes only after they enter its field of view, whereas panoramic video records the surroundings in every viewing direction and has served as an intermediate representation of the world state in recent world models. Learning this task therefore requires synchronized POV and panoramic videos of interacting players together with their actions, yet no existing dataset provides this combination in Minecraft, an established testbed in which players act independently in a shared, modifiable 3D world. We present PAWA, a dataset and framework for action-conditioned panoramic multiplayer world modeling. The dataset pairs each player's POV video with world-stabilized panoramic video and aligned actions. Its distributed pipeline decouples CPU gameplay capture from GPU rendering, scales beyond 64 simultaneous players, and re-renders each recorded session under new observation configurations without replaying the gameplay. On this dataset, we develop a dual-tower model that jointly predicts POV and panoramic video and couples the two streams through cross-attention that aligns tokens observing the same direction in a shared world frame. We further introduce a quadratic-phase player encoding that provides many more player codes than existing rotary codes at the same embedding dimension. Experiments show that PAWA outperforms state-of-the-art multiplayer world models in POV prediction quality while also producing high-fidelity panoramic predictions. The dataset and collection pipeline are open source to support further research on multiplayer world models.

papers.title: OneLA: Learning Many Worlds from Latent Actions
papers.abstract: Learning world models across diverse domains calls for a unified control space, yet ac- tion interfaces vary across domains and action annotations are often scarce. Latent ac- tions learned directly from videos offer a promising way to establish such a space without explicit action supervision. However, learning shared latent actions across domains re- mains challenging, as variations in appearance, embodiment, and dynamics can entangle domain-specific visual cues with transferable transition structure. To this end, we intro- duce OneLA, a simple framework that learns continuous latent actions through a shared orthogonal dictionary and a common predictive objective, without task-specific designs or cross-domain alignment losses during latent action pretraining. These latent actions pro- vide a shared conditioning interface for world models, with lightweight adapters mapping native control commands into the same space. Conditioned on latent actions and the cur- rent visual state, the world model predicts context-dependent transitions for controllable rollout. OneLA improves action readout across domains and reduces action cycle-transfer rotation error by 24.8% over the strongest evaluated baseline. A joint-training comparison further shows a 20.5% improvement in Human Preference Score v3 (HPSv3) for real- scene generation. These results suggest a path toward general-purpose world models that learn from diverse videos and support flexible control through latent action space.

papers.title: In-Context Batch Black-box Optimization via Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Batch black-box optimization is important for expensive systems where many candidates can be evaluated in parallel, yet only a few rounds of evaluation are affordable. In this regime, effective batch construction must identify multiple promising regions while avoiding redundant evaluations, and conventional Bayesian optimization can require increasingly difficult batch-selection procedures as the batch size grows. We introduce Flow Matching for Thompson-Sampling Refinement (FMTR), an amortized approach that learns offline a continuous, history-conditioned proposal distribution from which variable-size batches can be sampled. FMTR is trained offline by conditional flow matching on Thompson-sampling argmaxes refined toward high-value regions via a horizon-dependent Langevin pushforward map, adapting the exploration-exploitation tradeoff over the optimization horizon. At test time, the model parameters remain fixed and batch generation requires neither task-specific surrogate refitting nor numerical acquisition optimization. FMTR achieves strong performance against batch BO and in-context baselines on synthetic and real-world benchmarks, while substantially reducing the computational cost of batch selection.

papers.title: Feasibility of a Patient-Specific Digital Twin for Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt Trajectory Planning
papers.abstract: Catheter obstruction is the commonest cause of shunt failure; freehand insertion at Keen's point leaves the tip free in cerebrospinal fluid in only one case in ten. We built a digital twin that reconstructs skull, scalp, ear and ventricles from preoperative CT by deterministic geometry, searches every entry around Keen's point for the perpendicular trajectory with the longest intraventricular length under safety constraints, and returns the plan as two ruler measurements from the ear and two depths. Executed freehand in 11 consecutive adults (IDEAL Stage 2a), it achieved Hayhurst Grade 1 placement in 10 of 11 against 22 of 213 historically (p = 9 x 10^-9), median entry and angular deviations 2.5 mm and 5.9 degrees, 1.4 cm more intraventricular catheter than Keen's point, and no intraoperative complication. The technique was unchanged; the gain came from choosing entry and depth per patient. Whether it lowers revision is the next stage's hypothesis.

papers.title: Sequential Learning-Based Physics-Informed Neural Network Modeling for Parameter Estimation on a Power Converter
papers.abstract: A staged physics-informed neural network (PINN) is proposed for identifying the inductance, capacitance and parasitic resistances of a DC buck converter from time-domain data. Gradients are released in the order of L to C to rL to rC, a sequence derived from sensitivity analysis. The five-stage schedule recovers L and C to within 5% and the series ESR to 10%, while a three-stage variant attains the same accuracy 11% faster. An 84 factorial sweep confirms that the trained PINN remains accurate for simultaneous 8% perturbations of all four components, achieving a waveform RMSE of 2.6 x 10-2 over 5 ms-an order-of-magnitude better than a simultaneous-training baseline.

papers.title: Minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap of continuous Markov chains, with applications to empirical concentration bounds
papers.abstract: We study the minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap $γ_{ps}$ of a Markov chain from the observation of a single trajectory. Extending earlier works on finite-state space chains by Wolfer and Kontorovich (2024), we provide an estimator in the case of a compact, continuous state-space. Our estimator appears to be minimax-optimal on the class of chains with a transition operator with Lipschitz density, up to logarithmic terms. Our estimator, combined with Paulin's version of Bernstein inequality, allows to derive empirical concentration inequalities for Markov chains. This unlocks many applications, from confidence intervals, to active learning and generalization bounds. In particular, for rested bandits with Markov rewards, we provide a version of UCB with a regret bound similar to the one in the iid case, without assuming any knowledge on the pseudo-spectral gap of the chains.

papers.title: Neurosymbolic Learning of Interpretable World Models
papers.abstract: World models aim to learn compact representations of an environment from observations, enabling agents to predict future states and plan their behaviour. However, most existing approaches learn black-box representations, with limited ability to incorporate prior knowledge about the world. We introduce Concept-Grounded World Models (CGWMs), a neurosymbolic world model design that instead learns interpretable concept representations. We learn these concepts from observations using explicit and complete knowledge, expressed in temporal logic, that specifies the valid world states and the temporal relations governing their dynamics. Furthermore, we directly use this knowledge by formulating planning as differentiable reasoning, optimising the agent's actions by gradient ascent to satisfy a goal. We experimentally compare CGWM with a purely neural baseline and a neurosymbolic baseline on two game environments. We find that CGWMs ground concepts much more accurately, even over long horizons, resulting in significantly more robust planning both in and out of distribution.

papers.title: Convergence Rates of Gaussian Process Thompson Sampling for Efficient Global Optimization
papers.abstract: Efficient global optimization aims to identify a global optimum of an expensive black-box function within a limited evaluation budget $N$. We investigate the convergence rates of Gaussian process Thompson sampling (GP-TS) under noiseless observations, assuming a fixed objective function in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). For Matérn kernels with smoothness parameter $ν$ in dimension $d$, we establish a worst-case expected simple-regret upper bound of $O(N^{-ν/d}\sqrt{\log N})$ for both discrete GP-TS on sufficiently fine grids and its continuous counterpart. For the continuous implementation, we develop a nested-grid argument to control posterior sample paths over the entire domain. We further establish matching lower bounds of $Ω(N^{-5/2}\sqrt{\log N})$ for both implementations under a fixed one-dimensional Matérn-$5/2$ kernel, demonstrating that the logarithmic penalty is intrinsic to standard GP-TS in this setting. Motivated by this limitation, we propose Gaussian Process Capped Thompson Sampling (GP-CTS), which caps posterior sample paths using a valid RKHS norm upper bound while preserving optimism. This modification successfully eliminates the logarithmic penalty and achieves the minimax-optimal rate $Θ(N^{-ν/d})$ for both discrete and continuous implementations.

papers.title: CTIA-ODE: Continuous-Time Inter-Variable Attention for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Although multivariate time series forecasting has broad application prospects, effectively incorporating exogenous variables remains challenging. Prevailing discrete-time architectures often impose rigid temporal alignment across heterogeneous variables, which may limit their ability to capture continuously evolving external effects. To address this limitation, we introduce CTIA-ODE, a continuous-time forecasting framework centered on Continuous-Time Inter-Variable Attention (CTIA). Specifically, CTIA is embedded within an ordinary differential equation (ODE) solver, enabling the continuously evolving endogenous trajectory to dynamically query a static exogenous context along the integration path without requiring explicit temporal alignment. To improve the stability of the continuous latent dynamics, we further introduce a dual-stabilization strategy: architecturally, a Linear Residual Augmentation (LRA) module provides a macroscopic trend anchor, while an Outlier-Robust Hybrid Loss (ORHL) mitigates the influence of heavy-tailed anomalies during optimization. Extensive experiments across eight real-world datasets demonstrate that CTIA-ODE achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance across diverse datasets and prediction horizons, while maintaining a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off with a compact memory footprint and low inference latency, particularly under long-horizon forecasting settings. Anonymous code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CTIA-ODE-15A6/.

papers.title: What Matters for World Modeling in Vision-Language-Action Models?
papers.abstract: Integrating world models into Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) has emerged as a promising direction, enabling policies to anticipate future dynamics beyond reactive observation-to-action mapping. However, existing approaches vary simultaneously in their world representations, integration paradigms, and policy backbones, making it difficult to determine what truly matters for effective world model integration. To disentangle these factors, we categorize existing efforts into four representative paradigms, namely Implicit Future Alignment, Explicit Future Query, MoT Future Expert, and External World Predictor. We instantiate each within a unified framework and systematically evaluate these paradigms with diverse world representations and policy backbones across in-domain, out-of-domain, long-horizon, dynamic, few-shot, and real-world settings. Our study yields four main findings: 1) world representation effectiveness is paradigm-dependent, whereas 2D semantic representations offer robust, cross-paradigm gains; 2) no single paradigm is universally optimal, yet the decoupled MoT Future Expert offers competitive overall performance, particularly in OOD robustness; 3) world modeling consistently benefits policies built on standard VLMs, while decoupled designs exhibit greater compatibility with pretrained VLAs; and 4) world modeling improves performance over action-only baselines across multiple settings, with notable gains on long-horizon and dynamic tasks. Project page and video demonstrations are available at https://dylanmqs.github.io/WM-in-VLAs/.

papers.title: Enhancing Latent World Models with Associative Memory
papers.abstract: World models trained via latent dynamics offer a scalable path for embodied planning, yet existing methods suffer from representational collapse, computational overhead, and limited long-horizon capability. We introduce a memory-enhanced latent world model that augments JEPA-style prediction with a content-addressable memory bank. Our approach learns high-level representations directly from observations, operating at multiple temporal scales within a shared latent space, and conditions predictions via adaptive layer normalization. To prevent collapse and ensure effective memory usage, we design two complementary losses that encourage slot diversity and balanced temporal utilization. Experiments on PushT, Tworoom, Reacher, and OGBCube demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance with a lightweight architecture, outperforming conventional latent world models on long-horizon planning tasks.

papers.title: E2DRL: End-to-End Differentiable Reinforcement Learning for 3D Obstacle Avoidance in Quadruped Robots
papers.abstract: Differentiable reinforcement learning shows strong promise for robot policy learning, but its application to legged locomotion has remained limited to blind walking or simulated 2D tasks. Extending it to end-to-end visual obstacle avoidance is challenging because hard collision constraints and early termination upon contact corrupt first-order gradients, trapping optimizers in local minima. We present E2DRL, which addresses this with a soft differentiable obstacle-interaction formulation: penetration penalties across multiple body keypoints with velocity-conditioned stop-gradient shaping to provide the first-order training signals for 3D obstacle avoidance. To realize a deployable perception-control system, a privileged teacher trained via Soft Analytic Policy Optimization (SAPO) in a differentiable simulator is distilled into a recurrent depth-based student via DAgger, then blended with a base locomotion policy using a terrain-aware gating module for deployment. In simulation, E2DRL achieves higher sample efficiency than PPO and demonstrates superior velocity-tracking performance and 3D obstacle-avoidance capability compared with both PPO and Duality-based DCBF NMPC. We present the first sim-to-real validation of end-to-end differentiable RL for 3D obstacle avoidance on a Unitree Go2 in static and dynamic environments.

papers.title: PolyMorph: Learning Locomotion Policy for Cross-Embodiment Adaptation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning has enabled robust locomotion for legged robots, but learned policies are typically tied to a specific robot morphology and require additional engineering when the number of legs, actuators, or mechanical properties change. We present PolyMorph, a morphology-conditioned framework that learns a single locomotion policy for heterogeneous legged robots. PolyMorph converts each robot's URDF into joint-link modules and combines a recurrent encoder, graph-based Transformer, and per-joint decoder to generate actions across variable leg counts and joint configurations. To improve training stability, PolyMorph uses morphology-normalized rewards, adaptive robot sampling, and URDF-derived PD-gain initialization. We evaluate PolyMorph in simulation across bipedal, tripedal, and quadrupedal robots, including unseen morphology variants and platforms, and deploy the policy on real quadruped platforms operated in multiple configurations. The results show that a single PolyMorph policy generalizes across diverse robot morphologies without per-robot policy retraining.

papers.title: Back on Track: Deployment-time Policy Improvement via World Model Planning
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art visuomotor policies are increasingly capable of executing complex tasks, yet can fail during deployment in ways they cannot predict or recover from on their own. Improving their performance and robustness typically requires collecting more data, retraining, or modifying the policy architecture, all of which are time- and resource-intensive in practice. We instead propose an offline-trained monitoring-and-intervention framework that improves a policy during deployment using only black-box query access. From a limited set of labeled on-policy rollouts, we learn a policy-conditioned liveness value that measures the nominal policy's progress toward task completion; we additionally train a compact latent world model using these rollouts together with play data. At deployment, the liveness value continuously monitors execution. When it detects a loss of progress, a short-horizon planner searches the world model for corrective actions using the same value as its planning objective, after which control returns to the nominal policy. We evaluate our method on the LIBERO-Goal task suite and on a Franka Panda manipulator, using the vision-language-action model $π_{0.5}$ and a diffusion policy as nominal policies, and demonstrate significant improvements in task success rates, while supporting real-time control. Additional results and videos are available on the project website (https://policy-improvement-wm.pages.dev/).

papers.title: VLRLA: Deployment-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models through In-Context Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models connect visual perception and language understanding with robot control, providing a foundation for instruction-conditioned manipulation. However, conventional pretrained VLA policies lack a mechanism for gradual adaptation through accumulated interaction experience during deployment. We therefore propose VLRLA, a general framework that equips existing VLA models with \textit{in-context reinforcement learning} capabilities for deployment-time adaptation. Our approach augments a VLA model with a reinforcement learning module that learns from historical observations, actions, rewards, and termination signals. During deployment, the policy gradually refines its action generation and progressively improves task success while keeping model parameters fixed. Our approach is also designed for general applicability and compatibility with diverse learning history construction strategies and model training pipelines. Finally, through extensive experiments, we systematically investigate the learning properties of VLRLA in simulation and demonstrate its ability to adapt to unseen scenarios during real-world deployment.

papers.title: CktHGVAE: A Symmetric Design/State Heterogeneous Graph Variational Autoencoder for Transistor-level Analog/Mixed-signal Circuit Design and Analysis
papers.abstract: We propose CktHGVAE, a heterogeneous graph variational autoencoder for transistor-level analog/mixedsignal CMOS circuits that takes not only design variables but also state variables as its inputs and outputs. With a single hyperparameter configuration without topology-specific tuning, comparison between model-generated and SPICE-simulated circuit operational states gives median R2 values above 0.9 for typical single-ended voltage amplifiers and the CMOS inverter, and 0.81-0.96 for differential amplifiers with larger datasets. Latent-space optimization in the PCA-reduced latent space with Bayesian optimization, evolutionary search, random search, and quasi-exhaustive search is demonstrated for a common-source voltage amplifier with NMOS input and resistive load, where the objective function is defined as a penalty for deviation from required circuit specifications. For each search strategy, 93.3 - 100% of all design candidates suggested by the model satisfy the required circuit specifications at the decoder output, and SPICE simulations verify that 90 - 100% of them indeed satisfy the requirements. The model pretrained on a batch of topologies can be transferred to unseen topologies without retraining at all, with zero-shot reconstruction median R2 values of 0.72-0.90 in three of four scenarios, including transfer from single-ended to differential topologies, although the transfer fidelity depends on the choice of pretraining topologies. Our demonstrations suggest that the proposed model can potentially serve as a basis for AMS CMOS circuit design automation.

papers.title: Digital Self-Interference Cancellation for In-Band Full-Duplex Systems Based on Transformer Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Digital-domain self-interference cancellation is essential in in-band full-duplex radios after passive suppression and analog cancellation. It is particularly challenging when the desired signal is strong relative to the residual self-interference. In this regime, conventional iterative digital cancellers update their coefficients from desired-signal-contaminated received samples and may suffer substantial performance degradation. This paper reformulates digital-domain self-interference cancellation as an operator-learning problem. The proposed framework learns the temporal evolution of the residual self-interference channel from historical observations and uses the learned operator together with the known local transmit signal to reconstruct the current residual self-interference. A Transformer neural operator is used to realize this framework. The resulting method is trained in a desired-signal-free setting and then applied in the presence of a desired signal. A continuity-based analysis characterizes the sensitivity of the learned operator to the resulting input perturbation. Numerical experiments in static and time-varying channels, including time-varying SIR conditions, demonstrate stable cancellation performance over a wide range of interference levels. At 30 dB SIR, the proposed method improves the cancellation performance by 5--15 dB over the considered conventional methods.

papers.title: State-Matched Sequence Conformal Prediction
papers.abstract: Sequential conformal prediction needs to decide which past errors should calibrate uncertainty for the current target. Recency and online error feedback are useful when recent observations remain relevant, but the recent past can be a poor reference when comparable states recur at nonadjacent times, with the recurrence pattern generally unknown. We propose State-Matched Sequence Conformal Prediction (SMSCP), which constructs an explicit one-sided local-linear state from pre-target information, uses state similarity to select a matched reference set of past calibration scores, and then applies the ordinary unweighted conformal order statistic. In contrast to existing approaches, SMSCP uses state similarity to identify calibration observations relevant to the target score quantile. This motivates a theoretical analysis of whether nearby states have comparable target score quantiles under temporal dependence. We establish control of the resulting conformal cutoff and characterize predictive information not captured by the chosen state. Simulations show that state matching is most effective when score-relevant states recur across nonadjacent times, while revealing settings in which its advantage weakens or reverses. Across solar irradiance and bike-demand benchmarks, SMSCP improves interval score over recency, weighted, adaptive, and HopCPT comparators, and achieves coverage closer to the nominal 0.90 level than ResCP on five of six benchmarks.

summary_zh.method: 构建局部线性状态，用状态相似性匹配历史校准分数并应用保形次序统计量。
summary_zh.result: 在太阳辐照与自行车需求基准上区间评分优于多种对比方法，覆盖率更接近0.90。

summary_en.result: State matching improves interval score over recency, weighted, adaptive, and HopCPT comparators on solar irradiance and bike-demand benchmarks, with coverage closer to the nominal 0.90 level than ResCP on five of six benchmarks.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments on time-series benchmark datasets with theoretical analysis of conformal cutoff control.

papers.title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
papers.abstract: Reticular chemistry allows metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) to be designed from their building units, yet their synthesis remains constrained by sparse experimental data, noisy crystallization outcomes, and the absence of benchmarks for comparing active-learning strategies. While data-driven approaches such as Bayesian optimization (BO) can improve synthesis success rates, selecting appropriate optimizers beforehand for mapping MOF crystallization landscapes remains largely empirical. Here we present ActMOF, an experiment-grounded benchmark for comparing search strategies in aluminum-carboxylate MOF synthesis. ActMOF is emulated from experimentally measured microwave syntheses with each encoded condition assigned a crystallinity index calculated based on diffraction peak intensity and full width at half-maximum. By benchmarking policies guided by Gaussian processes (GP), tree ensembles and large language models (LLM), ActMOF placed the GP family among the leading policies for active learning in sparse synthesis landscapes. It then demonstrated transferability by guiding the microwave synthesis of six reticularly related aluminum MOFs. All six campaigns gave crystalline products within a fixed budget of 12 experiments each, and established a reusable testbed for AI-driven MOF synthesis.

papers.title: Fully sequential Gaussian process regression for preference learning
papers.abstract: We study continuous global optimization problems in which the objective function cannot be directly evaluated; rather, we observe only which of two selected design points appears to perform better, subject to noise. Such comparisons complicate the use of Gaussian process regression because they yield non-Gaussian posteriors. We consider a fully sequential approximation, based on moment-matching, that yields a fast closed-form update of the metamodel's mean and covariance. We then propose DOVE, a fully sequential sampling policy that combines an information gain criterion with randomized sampling designed to control error accumulation. Under fairly standard regularity conditions, we prove convergence rates for both statistical error and expected simple regret that depend on kernel smoothness. To our knowledge, these are the first such rates for fully sequential approximate Bayesian inference in continuous global optimization.

summary_zh.result: 在标准正则条件下证明了统计误差与期望简单遗憾的收敛率，且依赖于核光滑度。

summary_en.result: Convergence rates for statistical error and expected simple regret are established under regularity conditions, depending on kernel smoothness.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical proofs of convergence rates; no numerical experiments or physical simulations are reported.

papers.title: One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models
papers.abstract: Latent world models are routinely selected, checkpointed and ablated on one-step prediction loss, on the assumption that a model which predicts the next latent better is a better model. In model-based RL this assumption is known to be unreliable; we ask whether it also fails for latent world models, where the training target is the model's own embedding and the loss is not expressed in interpretable units. We introduce a frozen-decoder protocol reporting one-step error in physical units, decomposed into the part already present in the encoder's representation and the part the predictor adds. Applying it to a recent end-to-end JEPA world model across three continuous-control environments, we move the metric by fine-tuning and measure goal-conditioned planning on the same checkpoints, with three training seeds and paired planning seeds throughout. Within one environment, a per-epoch ladder shows the relationship saturating after a single epoch: the first epoch improves fidelity by 32% and planning by 4.4 pp, but across the fifteen checkpoints that follow -- a further 15% fidelity improvement, monotone in every training seed -- the correlation between one-step error and planning success is r = -0.010. This is not a task-ceiling artifact: stratifying by a model-independent measure of training-data support, planning in the lowest-support stratum starts at 80%, leaving ample headroom, and is nonetheless flat from epoch 1 onward. Across environments the exchange rate is equally unstable: a 93% fidelity reduction on TwoRoom yields -0.7 pp of planning, while a 40% reduction on PushT yields +4.9 pp [+1.1, +8.9]. All results replicate under a decoder-free measure, latent drift. We also show that a matched continued-training control absorbs the entire fidelity gain we had attributed to an auxiliary objective.

papers.title: Probabilistic Physics Digital Twin for Human-Robot Interaction
papers.abstract: Digital twins are increasingly used in robotics to simulate interactions, predict action outcomes, and support planning. However, constructing accurate digital twins requires precise estimates of physical properties such as mass, friction, and center of mass, which are often difficult to obtain in real-world environments. We propose probabilistic digital twins, which represent uncertain physical properties as probability distributions rather than fixed values. By simulating actions across these distributions, the twin predicts a range of possible outcomes and their likelihoods. These probabilistic simulations can guide both human and robot actions by identifying actions that are effective despite physical uncertainty. We demonstrate this framework through human-robot interaction scenarios, including interfaces that communicate simulated outcomes to users and robot planning strategies that explicitly account for uncertainty.

papers.title: SonoWorld: Towards Interactive Pose-Controllable Ultrasound World Models
papers.abstract: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. Existing approaches rely on robot-tracked poses and latent-space prediction, but do not directly generate the observations required for interactive control. We propose SonoWorld, a causal ultrasound world model that learns video dynamics from unlabeled clinical videos and grounds them to 6-DoF control using a small set of freehand clinical scans tracked with an EM sensor. SonoWorld is trained in three stages: pretraining a latent-action-conditioned video diffusion model on around 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ ultrasound frames; grounding the learned video dynamics to metric probe poses with a small EM-tracked thyroid dataset; and applying distribution matching distillation to enable causal, long-horizon autoregressive generation with selectively caching eviction tokens at inference time. We evaluate controllability through pose-following fidelity, round-trip consistency, and axis-specific control under synthetic actions on held-out tracked scans, and further validate it with a user study. In model-based action discrimination, SonoWorld correctly ranks the target-directed probe motion over an equal-magnitude opposite motion in up to 74.8% of trials. To our knowledge, SonoWorld is the first causal, pose-controllable ultrasound world model learned primarily from freehand clinical videos, providing a data-driven interactive environment for robotic ultrasound data acquisition and policy evaluation.

papers.title: Enzymatic cross-linking collagen-based bioink for 3D bioprinting of endometrial model with endometrial epithelial organoids
papers.abstract: The human endometrium, a dynamic tissue responsive to sex hormones, plays a pivotal role in female reproduction and menstrual cycling, comprising diverse cell populations including epithelial and stromal cells. The development of in vitro endometrial models holds substantial potential for tissue repair, drug discovery, and disease modeling. However, the construction of biomimetic structural in vitro models capable of supporting long-term culture and preserving relevant biological functions has been hindered by limitations in both material properties and fabrication strategies. Here, an enzymatically cross-linked collagen-based bioink was developed, enabling extrusion bioprinting with favorable printability, biocompatibility, and bioactivity. The enzyme-catalyzed cross-linking process was optimized through room-temperature pre-crosslinking, and its evolution was described using a storage modulus ( G′ )-time kinetic model, enabling prediction of the printable window and reliable fabrication of three-dimensional (3D) constructs. Then, monoculture and co-culture systems of endometrial epithelial organoids (EEOs) and endometrial stromal cells (ESCs) embedded in collagen-based hydrogels were established. Utilizing the bioink and printing strategy, an in vitro endometrial model was 3D bioprinted, exhibiting sustained viability (≥11 days) and hormone-responsive functions comparable to or showing enhanced functional characteristics relative to commonly used Matrigel-based or collagen-based systems. This biomimetic platform provides a physiologically relevant in vitro model for investigating endometrial biology, elucidating pathological mechanisms, and facilitating drug screening applications.

papers.title: A Systematic Benchmark of Physics-Informed Neural NetworkStrategies for Stiff Ion Transport in Lithium Symmetric Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract The Poisson–Nernst–Planck (PNP) system governs ion transport in lithium-ion battery electrolytes and presents a canonical stiff coupled PDE challenge: extreme coefficient ratios, sharp electric double-layer boundary layers, and nonlinear coupling between the Poisson and Nernst–Planck equations. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are appealing because they require no mesh and handle forward and inverse problems in one framework, but spectral bias and multi-task loss imbalance have limited their accuracy on stiff PNP systems. We present the first systematic, simulation-only benchmark of eleven PINN configurations, organised into four strategy groups (adaptive loss weighting, spectral bias mitigation, spatio-temporal decomposition, and physics enrichment), on a physically parametrised one-dimensional PNP model for a lithium symmetric cell, implemented in NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo Sym and validated against a high-resolution finite volume method reference. Root-mean-square errors span 10⁻² to 10⁻⁴: Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) adaptive weighting achieves the lowest errors (RMSE = 6.6×10⁻⁴ for anion concentration), while the balanced residual decay rate (BRDR) scheme matches NTK within 10% RMSE for concentrations while reducing wall-clock time by 3.2 ± 0.4 h per run. Loss landscape geometry corroborates the RMSE ranking. An open-source PhysicsNeMo Sym implementation is released for reuse in electrochemical modelling.

papers.title: Surrogate Computational Homogenization Enhanced by Partition‐of‐Unity RBF Interpolation With Decision Trees
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study enhances a framework of surrogate computational homogenization (SCH) using decision tree‐based partition‐of‐unity radial basis function (PU‐RBF) interpolation for three‐dimensional finite‐deformation two‐scale analysis. The method addresses the scalability limitation of global RBF interpolation for large numerical material test (NMT) datasets by partitioning the strain space into overlapping subdomains with a binary‐tree strategy and training local RBF interpolants blended by smooth partition‐of‐unity weights. This local‐global construction reduces training cost while preserving a continuously differentiable stress response, enabling consistent tangent evaluation in implicit finite element solvers. For hyperelastic composite unit‐cell problems, the SCH model is trained with datasets exceeding samples, reconstructs database responses with high fidelity, and reproduces ‐level trends in both macroscopic and localization analyses with improved computational efficiency. Because it is nonintrusive at the constitutive‐update level, the surrogate is straightforward to integrate into standard CAE workflows. The present model is interpolation‐based and therefore intended for deformation states covered by the training data.

papers.title: Bioprinting-Enabled Customization of Biohybrid Actuators: Scaling Dimensions and Functional Complexity
papers.abstract: Biohybrid actuators integrate living contractile cells with engineered materials, combining biological force generation with the structural and functional control offered by synthetic components. However, translating engineered muscle tissue into reproducible, high-performance biohybrid robots remains limited by tissue organization, matrix degradation, force transmission, and long-term functional stability. This review analyzes how biofabrication parameters and material properties influence tissue maturation and actuator-level performance, with particular emphasis on bioprinting. We compare muscle cell sources; extrusion-based, embedded, and light-assisted fabrication strategies; and scaffold biomaterials using reported structural and functional outcomes. We also evaluate electrical and optical activation and mechanical conditioning, distinguishing their roles in controlling contraction and promoting maturation. The comparison highlights a gap between architectural control during fabrication and reproducible robotic performance: methods that produce complex muscle constructs do not necessarily yield integrated devices with validated force transmission or locomotion. Tissue maturation, tissue–material interfaces, and nutrient transport emerge as closely coupled priorities for scaling functional constructs. We conclude with a framework for standardized benchmarking and discuss multimaterial printing, data-driven design, and feedback control as complementary routes toward more reproducible and capable biohybrid actuators.

papers.title: Dynamic Ultrasound Evaluation of Pelvic Floor Support Biomechanics After Transvaginal Mesh Implantation
papers.abstract: Quantitative evaluation of biomechanical changes in the pelvic floor support system following transvaginal mesh (TVM) implantation using dynamic pelvic floor ultrasound (PFUS), and exploration of the correlation between these changes and tissue repair outcomes, clinical symptom improvement, and the risk of postoperative complications. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 91 patients who underwent pelvic floor reconstruction surgery, divided into a TVM group (n=53) and a non-mesh traditional repair control group (n = 38). Dynamic pelvic floor ultrasound was used to measure the levator hiatus area (LHA), bladder neck descent (BND), retrovesical angle (RVA), and levator ani muscle integrity at rest, during the Valsalva maneuver, and during contraction. Biomechanical parameters such as pelvic floor surrogate tissue deformation index, surrogate support rigidity index, and load-bearing capacity were evaluated. Compared with the control group, the TVM group showed a more significant reduction in LHA during the Valsalva maneuver (ΔLHA reduction = 5.9 cm 2 vs. 3.3 cm 2 , P < 0.05) and a higher rate of levator ani muscle tear repair (89.5% vs. 57.1%, P = 0.011), indicating that TVM implantation effectively reduces pelvic floor surrogate tissue deformation index and improves load transfer efficiency. Additionally, the TVM group demonstrated better bladder neck stability and more favorable correction of the retrovesical angle. A combined concurrent association analysis based on postoperative PFUS parameters showed good discriminative ability for concurrent postoperative complications (Bootstrap-corrected AUC = 0.97; single-parameter AUC range: 0.88-0.96), though external validation is required to confirm generalizability. Preoperative LHA > 32.5 cm 2 or severe levator ani muscle tear were associated with TVM efficacy (AUC = 0.85). During the 3-month postoperative follow-up, transvaginal mesh repair demonstrated more favorable surrogate deformation index and surrogate support stiffness index compared with conventional autologous tissue repair, reflecting short-term imaging correlations. Dynamic pelvic floor ultrasound, utilizing geometric surrogate mechanical indices, may serve as an exploratory tool for biomechanical comparison, providing an objective and noninvasive imaging modality for preliminary postoperative efficacy assessment. These findings are based on simplified surrogate indices and short-term data, and long-term follow-up is still warranted to monitor delayed mesh-related complications.

papers.title: Physicochemical and biological profiles of a human donor plasma fractioning by-product
papers.abstract: Background. By-products of human donor plasma fractionation often possess untapped potential for regenerative medicine. However, they are frequently excluded from further technological processing, and a comprehensive physicochemical and biological characterization remains lacking – a gap that hinders the development of novel, effective biomaterials. Objective. To perform an integrated physicochemical and biological analysis of fibrinogen-containing precipitate No. 1 (FР No. 1) – a by-product of donor plasma fractionation – and to evaluate its potential as a raw material for biomedical applications. Materials and Methods. A multi-method approach was employed, including Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, UV spectrophotometry, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), SDS‑PAGE electrophoresis, quantitative determination of protein mass fraction, assessment of fibrinogen extraction yield in citrate buffer and phosphate-buffered saline (37 °C, 5 hours), as well as in vitro biological testing on human dermal fibroblast cultures. Results. FP No. 1 was found to preserve the structural integrity of fibrinogen with low levels of impurities. The lyophilizate formed porous fibrin matrices with pore sizes ranging from 100 to 180 μm. Cell viability upon contact with the material reached 96.5 % (p 0.05), confirming the absence of cytotoxicity. The protein mass fraction in the dry substance was 77 %. Under optimal extraction conditions, the fibrinogen yield reached 21.9 % (citrate buffer) and 21.5 % (phosphate-buffered saline). Conclusion. FP No. 1 represents a highly promising secondary protein raw material for the development of bioinks for 3D bioprinting, wound dressings, and tissue-engineered constructs. These findings strongly advocate for the rational reintegration of plasma fractionation by‑products into high‑technology biomedical applications.

papers.title: Guideline-Concordant Answer Quality of Five Large Language Models on Indication Criteria for Total Hip Arthroplasty in Hip Osteoarthritis: A Single-Run Benchmark Against the 2021 German S3 Guideline (EKIT-Hip)
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hip osteoarthritis (OA) is a highly prevalent musculoskeletal disorder associated with substantial functional impairment and healthcare burden. Although evidence-based clinical practice guidelines exist, including the 2021 guideline of the German Society for Orthopaedics and Trauma Surgery (DGOU), their implementation in routine practice remains incomplete. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly consulted for guideline-related information, but the concordance of their answers with guideline recommendations is uncertain. This benchmark study evaluated the guideline concordance, comprehensiveness and length of answers generated by five widely used LLMs to questions derived from the 2021 German S3 guideline on evidence- and consensus-based indication criteria for total hip arthroplasty in hip OA (EKIT-Hip; AWMF register no. 187-001; lead society DGOU). It did not evaluate the effectiveness or safety of clinical decision support. Methods: In a cross-sectional, single-run benchmark study, 26 structured, context-free questions covering five of the six thematic complexes of the guideline (diagnosis and imaging; assessment of the level of suffering; evaluation of alternative therapeutic options; contraindications; optimisation of modifiable risk factors) were derived from the guideline recommendations and submitted between 9 November 2024 and 25 February 2025 through the consumer web interfaces of five LLM-based systems (GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, Gemini Advanced and Consensus Premium), yielding 130 responses (one per system–question pair, each in a newly initiated chat session). Responses were evaluated by three board-certified orthopaedic surgeons blinded to model identity, using a four-point accuracy scale and a five-point comprehensiveness scale. Only a single consensus score per response was recorded, so inter-rater reliability could not be assessed. Response length was quantified in words and characters and benchmarked against the corresponding guideline text. Because all systems answered the same questions, ratings were analysed as paired, question-clustered data with cumulative-link mixed models (random intercept for question), Friedman and Cochran’s Q tests and question-level cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals; unpaired analyses were retained as sensitivity analyses. Results: Accuracy differed across systems (cumulative-link mixed model, likelihood-ratio χ2(4) = 49.0, p < 0.0001; paired Friedman χ2(4) = 41.7, p < 0.0001; unpaired Kruskal–Wallis sensitivity analysis H = 35.6, p < 0.0001). Mean accuracy was highest for GPT-4o (3.69 ± 0.55) and GPT-4 (3.62 ± 0.57), followed by GPT-4o mini (3.27 ± 0.78), Gemini Advanced (3.08 ± 0.84) and Consensus Premium (2.54 ± 0.71). Responses rated good or excellent accounted for 25/26 (96.2%) of GPT-4o and GPT-4 responses versus 15/26 (57.7%) for Consensus Premium. Comprehensiveness followed the same ordering (H = 33.0, p < 0.0001, ε2 = 0.23), with GPT-4o achieving the highest mean score (4.31 ± 0.79). In the cumulative-link mixed model, the odds of a higher accuracy rating relative to Consensus Premium were 51.8 (95% CI 12.4–215.9) for GPT-4o and 35.4 (95% CI 9.2–136.4) for GPT-4; GPT-4o and GPT-4 did not differ (OR 1.47, multiplicity-adjusted 95% CI 0.23–9.21), and their paired mean difference in accuracy (0.08 points, 90% CI −0.11 to 0.26) lay within an equivalence margin of ±0.5 points. Responses rated poor were observed for Consensus Premium (2/26) and Gemini Advanced (1/26) and not for the ChatGPT variants (0/26 each; exact 95% CI 0–13.2%), so a clinically relevant error rate cannot be excluded for any system. Response length differed markedly (Friedman χ2 = 47.3, p < 0.0001), ranging from 32.4 ± 11.5 words for Consensus Premium to 77.8 ± 24.9 words for GPT-4o, corresponding to 1.29-fold and 3.19-fold the length of the source guideline text, respectively. Conclusions: GPT-4o and GPT-4 received the highest ratings for accuracy and comprehensiveness in this single-run benchmark of static, context-free questions. These data describe guideline-concordant answer quality only; they do not establish clinical decision-support effectiveness or safety and do not support unsupervised clinical use of any evaluated system. Evaluation with standardised patient cases, repeated version-controlled runs, clinician-in-the-loop designs and prospective safety endpoints is required.

papers.title: Sensitivity Stability Analysis of Physics-Informed Neural Networks in Topology Optimization: PINN vs Gradient-Enhanced PINN
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have attracted considerable interest as mesh-free, differentiable alternatives to finite element solvers in topology optimization pipelines. However, their practical utility is undermined by a fundamental instability in the sensitivity fields they produce: higher-order spatial derivatives computed via automatic differentiation exhibit high variance and spatial inconsistency, causing gradient-based design updates to diverge and producing irregular optimized layouts. This paper presents a systematic sensitivity stability analysis comparing standard PINNs and gradient-enhanced PINNs (gPINNs) as structural solvers within a SIMP-based topology optimization framework. We evaluate four statistical measures of sensitivity quality — mean, median, standard deviation, and maximum variance — across 50 optimization iterations on three benchmark beam configurations (cantilever, simply supported, and fixed–fixed). Results demonstrate that the gPINN formulation achieves a 94.35\% reduction in mean sensitivity variance relative to standard PINNs, with correspondingly smoother optimized topologies consistent with classical finite element benchmarks. A post-filtering analysis further shows that gPINN requires substantially less external smoothing to achieve stable optimization convergence, confirming that gradient enhancement provides intrinsic rather than post-hoc stability. These findings establish sensitivity stability as a critical and previously underexamined criterion for evaluating physics-informed surrogates in structural optimization.

papers.title: Finite Element Analysis of Drone Impact on a Rotating Aircraft Engine Fan: Sensitivity to Blade Material and Impact Velocity
papers.abstract: An explicit finite element study examined the sensitivity of a rotating aircraft-engine fan to blade material and drone impact velocity. A complete 20-blade rotor and a deformable, equivalent-material quadcopter were modelled in ANSYS/LS-DYNA. Ti-6Al-4V, Ti-6242 and AA2024-T3 blades were assessed at 30, 60 and 100 m/s with an initial fan angular velocity of 283 rad/s. Nine frictional simulations and one Ti-6Al-4V frictionless case at 100 m/s were evaluated using stress, equivalent plastic strain, directional displacement, erosion and energy histories. Ti-6Al-4V produced the lowest maximum blade plastic strain at each velocity; AA2024-T3 values were 11.6–26.9 times greater despite lower equivalent stress. No fan elements were deleted, whereas drone deletion occurred in every case. The maximum-history reduction in surviving-drone kinetic energy increased with velocity, but the highest velocity did not produce the largest plastic strain in every material. Including friction increased maximum plastic strain by a factor of 6.46 in the sensitivity case. The results highlight multi-blade chronology and complementary response measures within the adopted model; local impact convergence and configuration-specific experimental validation were not established.

papers.title: Neural Network-Based Surrogate Modelling for Accelerated and Accurate Thermal History Prediction in Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) of Ti-6Al-4V alloy
papers.abstract: Abstract Thermal history during wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) governs microstructural evolution and mechanical properties, but FEM simulations used to predict it are too computationally expensive for iterative process optimisation. Prior surrogate models have also rarely reported which input features drive their predictions, leaving physical interpretability largely unaddressed. We developed an interpretable feed-forward neural network surrogate (FFNN) for fast thermal-cycle prediction in WAAM of Ti-6Al-4V, built in PyTorch and trained on ~65 million spatiotemporal points from FEM simulation. The model achieved a training R² of 0.998 and RMSE of 8.7 °C across ~25-2000 °C. On unseen current levels, it generalized well (R² = 0.9968–0.9971, RMSE = 10.9-13.4 °C), with per-current RMSE ranging from 7.7 °C to 23.9 °C across all four monitoring points. Feature analysis, re-verified on the full test set, identified cumulative deposition time, torch position, and arc source distance as the dominant predictors; current ranked lowest under both permutation and SHAP importance, though partial-dependence analysis confirmed this reflects smaller effect size not physical unimportance with current exerting a real, monotonic influence that interacts with build height. The FFNN-surrogate cuts computation time substantially, offering a practical tool for rapid process analysis and optimisation in Ti-6Al-4V WAAM.

papers.title: Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Analysis of Stone‐Column‐Reinforced Composite Foundations Constrained by Static Load Tests
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate identification of constitutive parameters for stone‐column‐reinforced composite foundations is essential for deformation analysis and settlement prediction of clay‐core rockfill dams. However, the parameters of the Duncan‐Chang model are difficult to determine directly under field conditions, whereas conventional inversion methods relying on repeated finite element (FE) analyses are computationally expensive. To address this issue, this study proposes a surrogate‐assisted parameter inversion framework constrained by static load tests in the stone‐column‐reinforced composite foundation of a planned clay‐core rockfill dam in Rwanda. Response samples under staged loading were generated using FE simulations, and a surrogate model was introduced into the inversion loop as a computational substitute for repeated FE analyses, thereby improving inversion efficiency. By jointly calibrating settlement responses under multiple load levels, the Duncan‐Chang model parameters governing the overall load‐settlement behaviour of the composite foundation were identified. Furthermore, uncertainty analysis was conducted for a representative test column to obtain the posterior distributions of the key parameters and the parameter‐induced posterior prediction intervals of the load‐settlement response. The identified parameters were further validated through FE back‐analysis and dam‐scale settlement prediction. The results show that the proposed framework can satisfactorily reproduce the load‐settlement response observed in static load tests while substantially reducing the computational cost. This study demonstrates that surrogate‐assisted parameter inversion constrained by static load tests provides a practical and robust approach for parameter identification in stone‐column‐reinforced composite foundations, while maintaining a favourable balance between efficiency and engineering applicability.

papers.title: Design of an intralayer data-based controller for laser powder bed fusion processing
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a data-based approach to reduce defect-prone process conditions during the additive manufacturing of Ti-6Al-4V alloy parts using the laser powder bed fusion technique. The focus is on controlling melt pool emissions intensity used as a temperature-related proxy generated as the laser interacts with the alloy powder to avoid processing conditions which generate defects such as lack-of-fusion (LOF) or keyhole porosity. A data-based controller is developed using photodiode signals from the melt pool emissions to predict future melt pool data and then update the control input accordingly. The prediction is achieved by estimating the Markov parameters and constructing a finite impulse response (FIR) model of the process. This controller, termed the data-based predictive FIR-based proportional controller, adjusts the laser energy input by applying a proportional correction to deviations of the melt pool emissions from their setpoint, thereby mitigating under- or overheating of the melt pool. The developed approach is investigated for the printing of spinal cage medical devices and evaluated through a closed-loop MATLAB simulation to assess its potential for intralayer control. A threshold-based anomaly detection approach is then employed to quantitatively evaluate the controller’s effectiveness in reducing defect-prone signal excursions. Results demonstrate a 99.98% reduction in the number of samples exceeding the defined thresholds within the studied layer after applying the controller, indicating the potential of the controller to reduce defect-prone process conditions associated with LOF and keyhole porosity if successfully deployed on the L-PBF system. Furthermore, closed-loop stability and sensitivity to control parameter variations are analysed.

papers.title: Direct Anterior or Posterolateral Approach for Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty? A Systematic Review of Early Recovery, Long-Term Outcomes, and Surgical Complications
papers.abstract: The optimal surgical approach for primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) remains debated. The direct anterior approach (DAA) has been associated with faster early recovery, whereas its potential advantages over posterior or posterolateral approaches (PA/PLA) in terms of longer-term outcomes and complications remain uncertain. This systematic review aimed to compare DAA with PA/PLA across early recovery, functional, perioperative, and complication-related outcomes. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched for primary comparative studies published from January 2005 to December 2025. Randomized and non-randomized studies comparing DAA with an identifiable PA/PLA group in adults undergoing primary THA were eligible. Companion publications from the same trial or cohort were consolidated into single study units. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for randomized studies and ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively. The search identified 2216 records; 111 reports underwent full-text assessment, 89 were eligible, and eight companion reports were consolidated, resulting in 81 primary comparative study units. Fourteen were randomized and 67 were non-randomized. Across the evidence base, DAA was frequently associated with modest advantages in selected early postoperative outcomes, including pain, mobilization, functional recovery, and hospital length of stay. These differences generally diminished with longer follow-up, with medium- to long-term functional outcomes largely comparable between approaches. Findings for operative time, blood loss, and individual complications were heterogeneous. No consistent overall advantage was identified for major complications, revision, or implant survival, although the approaches showed different profiles for specific complications. Interpretation of the observational evidence was limited particularly by confounding, patient selection, surgeon experience, and differences in perioperative pathways. DAA may accelerate selected aspects of early recovery after primary THA, but these advantages generally diminish over time. Current comparative evidence does not demonstrate a consistent long-term functional or major-complication advantage over contemporary PA/PLA. Surgical approach should therefore be individualized according to patient characteristics, surgeon experience, and institutional practice.

papers.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty in a Patient With Alpha-Gal Syndrome
papers.abstract: Alpha-gal syndrome (AGS) is an IgE-mediated reaction against galactose-ɑ-1,3-galactose, an oligosaccharide found in mammalian-derived foods and numerous medications containing animal products. AGS is an acquired condition brought about by a tick-borne illness that is increasing in prevalence in the United States. Managing this condition is particularly challenging in the surgical setting, where many commonly used hemostatic and analgesic agents contain animal-derived inactive ingredients. We describe a multidisciplinary approach taken to prevent triggering an allergic reaction in a patient with AGS who underwent total hip arthroplasty leading to a successful recovery. This case highlights important perioperative considerations in patients with AGS and describes a safe pathway to successful arthroplasty in this high-risk population.

papers.title: Correlation between vitamin D blood levels and implant success: a prospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Vitamin D is a fat-soluble hormone that can be produced in the skin by Ultra-Violet (UV) light exposure or acquired through diet. Vitamin D is currently of relevance to dentists placing dental implants because it plays a role in bone metabolism and controls the immune system. There is some evidence that the osseointegration process of dental implants is favorably correlated with the proper concentration of this prohormone. Several studies have demonstrated that vitamin D may be crucial for both the integration of the implant into bone tissue and the postoperative tissue repair process. Aim The aim of this study was to find out if there was a correlation between serum vitamin D levels and implant success. Methods This study was conducted on 100 patients divided into two equal groups who received single dental implant to restore single missing tooth. After implant placement, patients were not advised to receive any supplements for 3 months. Patient’s serum level of vitamin D was tested after 3 months of implant placement (osseointegration period). Clinical and radiographic assessment of dental implants were performed after 3 months postoperatively. Results Statistical analysis showed no statistical significance results ( P value 0.277) regarding the positive correlation between vitamin D levels and implant success/ failure, it also showed no statistical significance ( P value 0.663) regarding the relationship between Vitamin D levels and implant success/failure based on the implant location. Conclusion Serum vitamin D level has no direct effect on the success or failure of dental implants.

papers.title: Plasma Electrolytic Polishing of LPBF Ti-6Al-4V: Surface Integrity, Tensile Fatigue Behaviour of Solid Specimens, and FEA-Guided Stress Analysis of Gyroid Scaffolds
papers.abstract: This study presents an integrated computational–experimental approach to enhance the tensile fatigue life of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF)-fabricated Ti-6Al-4V Gyroid scaffolds for orthopedic implants. Scaffolds with 60–80% porosity were designed, and finite element analysis (FEA) was employed to analyze localized stress distribution, mechanical behavior, and crack initiation sites under compression, bending, and tensile loading. The FEA results showed that elastic modulus (2.6–8.0 GPa) and compressive yield strength (85.5–251.3 MPa) aligned with human bone requirements. The bending and tensile FEA identified that tensile stress concentrations at exterior node surfaces promoted crack initiation. The LPBF-induced surface roughness further intensified these stresses, accelerating crack nucleation and compromising fatigue life. To address this, plasma electrolytic polishing (PEP) was applied at 240 V for 15, 20, and 25 min on the LPBF Ti-6Al-4V solid tensile specimens and Gyroid scaffolds. To evaluate the effect of PEP on surface integrity and fatigue performance, roughness and tensile fatigue tests were performed on LPBF Ti-6Al-4V solid tensile specimens rather than on porous scaffolds. The PEP for 20 min significantly reduced the average roughness (Ra) from 17.85 ± 1.27 µm (as-built) to 2.84 ± 0.45 µm, with an improvement of 84.10%, while also showing the smooth quality of the Gyroid scaffolds. Consequently, the enhanced surface quality led to a 30.46% increase in the average tensile fatigue cycles to failure (Nf) (σmax = 800 MPa and R = 0.1) of the solid specimens compared to the as-built condition. This improvement indicates the PEP’s effectiveness in enhancing the material fatigue life through surface defect elimination, serving as surface- and material-level supporting evidence for the potential fatigue life improvement of PEP-treated Gyroid scaffolds.

papers.title: Assessment of Geometry-Dependent Dimensional and Surface Variability in Metal FFF Additive Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Material Extrusion (MEX)-based Additive Manufacturing (AM), particularly metal Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF), has gained attention for fabricating metal components due to its operational simplicity, cost-effectiveness, design flexibility, and reduced material waste. Compared with laser powder bed fusion, metal FFF offers lower thermally induced residual stress and avoids direct powder handling. However, dimensional accuracy and surface quality remain affected by process variability, shrinkage during sintering, and geometry-dependent material redistribution. Quantitative relationships among geometric features, dimensional deviation, and surface morphology are still limited. This study investigates geometry-dependent dimensional and surface variability in metal FFF parts using two stress-concentrator geometries: a plate with a circular hole and a specimen with a filleted transition. Geometric features, including hole diameter, fillet radius, and local curvature, were evaluated in relation to dimensional variability and surface roughness. The analysis used RMS-based dimensional error, PCA-based roughness indexing, regression, and clustering. The results showed that hole specimens had lower dimensional behavior, with ΔRMS values ranging from approximately 0.790% to 1.606%, whereas fillet specimens exhibited higher variability, with ΔRMS values ranging from 1.140% to 4.086%. Sensitivity analysis showed that the higher variability of the fillet geometry was primarily associated with the local curved transition rather than the specimen’s global dimensions. Regression indicated that surface roughness alone did not explain dimensional variability, while tensile strength provided an additional performance descriptor. Clustering further showed more compact response groupings for the hole specimens and more dispersed groupings for the fillet specimens, indicating the greater geometry sensitivity of the filleted transition. By combining the parameters studied, a framework was developed to provide a quantitative basis for assessing geometry-dependent variability and to support improved design guidelines for metal FFF parts with filleted transitions and stress-concentrating features.
