papers.title: Adaptive and uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling for reliability analysis of nonlinear dynamic systems
papers.abstract: Reliability analysis of nonlinear inelastic dynamic systems under uncertainty remains a critical challenge, owing to the path-dependent, high-dimensional nature of the problem. To this end, this paper proposes an adaptive and uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling framework comprising three synergistic components. The first component is the aLSTM–SNGP surrogate model, an uncertainty-aware surrogate for nonlinear dynamic systems that integrates an attention-enhanced LSTM (aLSTM) encoder with a Spectral-normalized Neural Gaussian Process (SNGP) predictor, jointly optimized through end-to-end co-training. The aLSTM encoder processes excitation sequences and system parameters together, capturing temporal dependencies while implicitly reducing dimensionality; the SNGP predictor provides scalable uncertainty-aware prediction through random Fourier feature approximation. The second component develops two surrogate-based failure probability estimation methods: Method I (aLSTM-SNGP-MCS) based on direct Monte Carlo simulation, and Method II (aLSTM-SNGP-IS) based on importance sampling with an adaptively constructed proposal density that concentrates sampling effort in failure-prone regions. The third component is an adaptive exploration–exploitation refinement strategy that iteratively refines the surrogate model by combining active learning with an alternating training scheme of full training and local fine-tuning. The framework is validated under stochastic seismic excitations through two examples: a numerical example based on a six-story nonlinear inelastic shear building model with Bouc-Wen hysteresis, and a practical engineering example based on a nine-story SAC steel frame represented by a nonlinear finite element model. Results demonstrate that both methods yield accurate failure probability estimates while significantly reducing the number of evaluations to the simulation model relative to crude Monte Carlo simulation, with Method II outperforming Method I.

papers.title: Advancing the Translational Pipeline: From In Vivo and In Vitro 2D Models to Next-Generation Cell Culture Models for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Modelling and Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Background: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is still a global health challenge, as there is no effective treatment due to the inadequacy of conventional experimental platforms for comprehending pathogenic mechanisms and developing therapy. Objectives: This review details the recent progress and clinical utility of next-generation iPSC-derived 3D in vitro systems integrated with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, multi-omics readouts, and AI-based machine learning, which are emerging as transformative platforms for recapitulating key ALS pathological hallmarks. Methods: A literature search was performed using PubMed and Web of Science, including only English-language publications. All the published papers collected covered the period from January 2015 to June 2026. Results: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) cerebral organoids, assembloids, and organ-on-a-chip technologies are revolutionizing research into ALS by providing a way to model the complex spatial organization, cellular heterogeneity, and neural network dynamics of the human brain. Moreover, recent bioengineering advancements enable the inclusion of functional neurovascular units, the integration of resident immune cells (microglia), and the use of 3D bioprinting to accelerate the functional maturation of age-related phenotypes. CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, OMICS, and machine learning improve tools for studying ALS and identifying therapeutic targets. Conclusions: Novel cell culture models may bridge the gap between preclinical animal models and human clinical trials and reduce the duration and costs of translation. Future work is likely to integrate bioprinting with organ-on-chip microfluidics, CRISPR-based genetic editing, and multi-omics readouts to build increasingly faithful, patient-specific ALS models for both basic research and precision therapeutics.

papers.title: Numerical Simulation Engines and Deep Learning Architectures for Inverse Design of Multilayer Metamaterials
papers.abstract: The inverse design of multilayer metamaterials —artificial structures with engineered electromagnetic, acoustic, thermal, or mechanical properties— represents a high-dimensional optimisation challenge that has driven the integration of deep learning into computational photonics and materials science. This paper presents a systematic literature review conducted under the PRISMA 2020 protocol, aimed at mapping the numerical simulation methods employed as forward engines or training data generators within deep learning-assisted inverse design pipelines. Starting from 392 records retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science over the 2010–2025 period, a multi-stage screening process based on a heuristic prioritisation index termed CARS (Citation-Adjusted Relevance Score) identified 44 core articles. Eleven distinct numerical methods were identified and organised into two conceptual layers: classical simulation engines (finite element method, topology optimisation, guided-mode expansion, adjoint method, and genetic algorithms) and deep learning architectures (tandem CNN, transformer, GAN, PINN, and diffractive neural networks). Results show a strong dominance of the electromagnetic-photonic domain (72%), accelerated growth of deep learning-based publications from 2022 onward, and a clear trend toward hybrid physics, data and learning pipelines. The review concludes by proposing a prioritised experimental roadmap for future research.

papers.title: Biomanufacturing Vascular Matrix-Mimetic Hydrogels from Quantified Arterial Micromechanics and Microstructure.
papers.abstract: The microstructural and micromechanical properties of the arterial extracellular matrix (ECM) are central to vascular cell behavior but are disrupted by disease and aging. Elastin and fibrillar collagens provide essential cues, yet the effects of disease-associated ECM remodeling on smooth muscle function remain poorly defined. Here, we imaged fibrillar ECM components across layers of healthy and hypertensive arteries in a large animal model and quantified their stiffness with submicron and piconewton resolution. These animal-derived data guided the fabrication of artery-mimetic hydrogels using image-derived 3D projection micro-stereolithography (µSTL) and thiol-ene clickable bioinks. The resulting hydrogels replicated fibril features down to 2 µm with emulated curvatures and tunable stiffness spanning physiological to pathological ranges (1-35 kPa). Systematic optimization of printing parameters, including light intensity, exposure time, monomer concentration, crosslinker type, optical configurations, and hydrogel swelling solutions, ensured high-fidelity structural replication. Vascular smooth muscle cells cultured on these hydrogels revealed that diseased ECM conditions promoted hypertrophy, impaired contractility, and reduced calcium responsiveness. Quantitative PCR showed reduced expression of contractile markers (MYH11, SMTN) and marked upregulation of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase) on hypertensive-mimetic matrices, implicating focal adhesion-dependent mechanotransduction in this response. This image-guided biofabrication platform enables precise engineering of vascular microenvironments for mechanistic studies of remodeling, therapeutic testing, and modeling of complex vascular disease states. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Arterial extracellular matrix stiffens and reorganizes in hypertension, yet in vitro models rarely reproduce these micron-scale changes. We measured layer-specific stiffness and fibrillar architecture in arteries from normotensive and hypertensive steers, a large animal model with fattening-induced hypertension. These data were directly translated into projection micro-stereolithography of thiol-ene hydrogels. The resulting matrices, high-fidelity 3D hydrogel prints, reproduced fibrillar features down to 2 µm with emulated curvatures and tunable stiffness spanning 1-35 kPa. Vascular smooth muscle cells cultured on hypertensive-mimetic matrices exhibited hypertrophic morphology, reduced calcium responsiveness and agonist-induced contractility, altered contractile-marker expression, and increased PTK2 expression, linking disease-associated matrix remodeling to altered mechanotransduction. This measurement-to-fabrication workflow provides a physiologically informed platform for mechanistic studies of vascular remodeling and evaluation of therapeutic responses.

papers.title: Reduced-Order Modeling of Hamiltonian Dynamics Based on Symplectic Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Abstract. We introduce a novel data-driven symplectic reduced-order modeling (ROM) framework for high-dimensional Hamiltonian systems that unifies latent-space discovery and dynamics learning within a single, end-to-end neural architecture. The encoder–decoder is built from Hénon neural networks (HénonNets) and may be augmented with linear G-reflector layers, yielding a structure-preserving symplectic embedding and an associated one-sided symplectic pseudo-inverse between the full and latent phase spaces. Latent dynamics are advanced by a symplectic flow map implemented as a HénonNet. This unified neural architecture ensures exact preservation of the underlying symplectic structure at the reduced-order level, significantly enhancing the fidelity and long-term stability of the resulting ROM. We validate our method through comprehensive numerical experiments on canonical Hamiltonian systems. The results demonstrate the method’s capability for accurate trajectory reconstruction, robust predictive performance beyond the training horizon and strong Hamiltonian preservation. These promising outcomes underscore the effectiveness and potential applicability of our symplectic ROM framework for complex dynamical systems across a broad range of scientific and engineering disciplines. The implementation associated with this work is publicly available at https://github.com/chenyongssss/Symp_NN .

papers.title: Robustifying Approximate Bayesian Computation
papers.abstract: Approximate Bayesian computation (ABC) is one of the most popular "likelihood-free" methods. These methods have been applied in a wide range of fields by providing solutions to intractable likelihood problems in which exact Bayesian approaches are either infeasible or computationally costly. However, the performance of ABC can be unreliable when dealing with model misspecification. To circumvent the poor behavior of ABC in these settings, we propose a novel ABC approach that is robust to model misspecification. This new method can deliver more accurate statistical inference under model misspecification than alternatives and also enables the detection of summary statistics that are incompatible with the assumed data-generating process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through several simulated examples, where it delivers more accurate point estimates and uncertainty quantification over standard ABC approaches when the model is misspecified. Additionally, we apply our approach to an empirical example, further showcasing its advantages over alternative methods.

papers.title: An improved physics-informed neural network for valuing American lookback options under regime-switching jump-diffusion models
papers.abstract: This study addresses the computational challenges inherent in valuing American lookback options within a regime-switching jump-diffusion (RSJD) framework. We first formulate the pricing problem as a system of coupled partial integro-differential equations (PIDEs) structured as linear complementarity problems (LCPs), rigorously capturing the interplay of path dependency, early exercise rights, and market regime transitions. To solve this complex free-boundary problem, we propose an improved physics-informed neural network (I-PINN). This novel architecture augments the standard PINN framework by incorporating a hard-coded terminal condition to guarantee theoretical consistency, a dynamic self-adaptive weighting scheme to balance the composite loss function, and the Fischer–Burmeister function to provide an exact semismooth reformulation of the LCP constraints. For accuracy assessment, the proposed method is benchmarked primarily against independently refined finite-difference reference solutions obtained from a reduced one-dimensional solver for floating-strike options and a full two-dimensional solver for fixed-strike options. The results show that the I-PINN attains competitive pricing accuracy, improved training stability relative to the standard PINN, and efficient post-training evaluation across the state domain. Furthermore, the practical applicability of the framework is validated through the accurate computation and analysis of key risk sensitivities, establishing it as a robust instrument for modern risk management.

papers.title: Uncertainty quantification-driven shear wave velocity prediction using a spatiotemporal Bayesian neural network
papers.abstract: Abstract Shear wave velocity (Vs) is a key parameter used for seismic data processing and evaluating oil and gas reservoirs. Conventional logging and machine learning methods are hampered by the provision of fixed Vs predictions, which limits their capacity to effectively quantify the uncertainty of predictions. Therefore, we propose a spatiotemporal Bayesian neural network (STBNN), which exploits the advantages of ensemble learning methods in processing logging data and Bayesian methods in modeling uncertainty. STBNN facilitates both accurate Vs predictions and a robust quantification of uncertainty. We initially perform a feature selection on logging data to identify logging-sensitive attributes as input features, and employ Monte Carlo dropout, a Bayesian approximation method, to determine both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties. These uncertainties are integrated into the STBNN framework, which reduces prediction uncertainty and enhances accuracy. Subsequently, we assess the model using a logging dataset derived from actual oil reservoirs, and evaluate its generalizability. The trained STBNN model is applied to an untrained exploration area to predict Vs and its associated uncertainties. Finally, we assess the influence of sample size on network epistemic uncertainty and devise a practical mitigation strategy. The results reveal that compared with spatiotemporal neural network and empirical models, the STBNN model achieves a higher accuracy of prediction. We establish that prediction uncertainty is primarily attributable to epistemic uncertainty, with higher uncertainty observed in areas with limited data. This prediction uncertainty can be effectively reduced by increasing the diversity of sample data. The proposed method delivers excellent Vs prediction results, whilst minimizing the risk of errors in the interpretation of logging.

papers.title: A Computational Workflow Integrating Explainable AI and Database Mining for the Prioritization of Antimicrobial Natural Products
papers.abstract: The escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance demands the discovery of antibacterial agents with unprecedented chemical scaffolds. Natural products have historically been the most prolific source of antibiotics, yet the vast majority of catalogued natural products remain untested for antimicrobial activity. Here we present Natural-Product Graph–language, Uncertainty-Aware Relational Discovery (NP-GUARD), a modular computational framework that reframes antimicrobial natural-product discovery as an uncertainty-aware, relational, multi-objective learning problem. NP-GUARD integrates six core components: provenance-tracked data curation, multi-view molecular representation, pathogen-conditioned multi-task prediction, explicit uncertainty quantification, stability-aware explainability, and conformal-Pareto prioritization, all consolidated within a queryable knowledge base. Of these components, the present study implements and benchmarks the data-curation, predictive, uncertainty, explainability and prioritization layers, including a first pathogen-conditioned masked multi-task graph model, while the full multi-view encoder and the knowledge base are specified for subsequent work. We report a proof-of-concept evaluation on public screening data forStaphylococcus aureus (38,995 compounds), Escherichia coli (2291) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (29,986), together with human cytotoxicity data and a 406,959-compound screening library from COCONUT. Under repeated scaffold-aware splitting, baseline models achieve strong discrimination (AUROC 0.78–0.93) but reveal substantial split-to-split variance in minority-class performance; class-conditional conformal prediction attains near-nominal per-class coverage; and feature attributions show only moderate stability across independently trained models (top-20 Jaccard 0.54), underscoring a critical caveat for explanation-driven discovery. Screening the COCONUT library validates the uncertainty-aware activity ranking, achieving an 87-fold enrichment of known antibiotics in the top 100 candidates (128-fold within the fully characterized named-compound stratum), although analogue-exclusion analysis shows this signal is dominated by rediscovery of training-like chemistry. The novelty-seeking Pareto layer yields a structurally diverse 90-compound shortlist spanning 72 scaffolds, deliberately steered toward unexplored chemotypes; we emphasize that the shortlist constitutes prioritized hypotheses for experimental testing, not validated actives. NP-GUARD provides a transparent, reproducible and decision-oriented foundation for prioritizing natural products for experimental validation.

papers.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and information needs regarding norovirus infection among parents of primary school students directly affected by outbreaks: a cross-sectional study in Hangzhou, China
papers.abstract: Background Norovirus outbreaks are prevalent in primary schools; however, few studies have specifically examined the parents directly impacted by these events. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted between January 2025 and March 2026. Parents from seven primary schools affected by norovirus outbreaks in Hangzhou, China, were invited to complete a self-administered online questionnaire. Data were collected on sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of norovirus pathogenesis, attitudes toward prevention and control, and information needs. Results A total of 322 valid responses were obtained (response rate 82.14%). Among respondents, 83.85% reported awareness of norovirus. The mean knowledge score regarding norovirus pathogenesis was 6.43 ± 1.91 out of 11 (58.45% correct), with only 14.07% attaining a “good” knowledge level (≥9 points). Attitude scores were high, with a rate of 88.22% of the maximum. Multivariable logistic regression identified educational attainment (bachelor’s degree or higher: OR = 6.27, 95% CI: 1.75–52.28), residence type (detached house: OR = 5.76, 95% CI: 1.48–6.18), and active information-seeking (OR = 24.60, 95% CI: 11.28–53.66) as factors independently associated with good knowledge level. Conclusion Parents directly affected by norovirus outbreaks demonstrated inadequate knowledge but held positive attitudes. Proactive information-seeking was the strongest predictor of good knowledge. Targeted health education, particularly through WeChat parent groups, is urgently required to bridge knowledge gaps and foster active learning.

papers.title: Direct and inverse problems for the Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation in a 2‐D model of a lattice
papers.abstract: Abstract This study expands the range of previously known physical models for the Korteveg-de Vries (KdV) family of equations. Based on the one-dimensional Fermi-Pasta–Ulam–Tsingou approach, we considered a model of nonlinear oscillations in a thin solid plate with a non-uniform crystal lattice and proved that compression waves propagate in this structure. These waves are described by the Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation (KP) with variable coefficients, which depend on the lattice structure. We proved that there is a broad class of the KP solutions for which the KP reduces to the KdV equation with variable coefficients. Since the KdV equation in this case is not precisely integrable, we considered the class of piecewise constant coefficients and proved the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for weak solutions. We proved that the integrals of the solution moments are well-defined. We formulated the inverse problems of determining the coefficients or some its combinations from these integrals and proved that there is no more than one solution to the problems. The results of modeling and numerical solution of the inverse problem confirm all theoretical studies. Computer simulations have shown that using the integrals of the solution moments is the correct method to select input data for the inverse problem. The results obtained demonstrate that developed algorithms restore the complex lattice structures when the initial wave is unknown. The study also solved the problems of detecting small dislocations and structural defects in the crystal lattice. These problems are typical for manufacturing and testing integrated circuits and microchips.

papers.title: BEYOND GRADES: RETHINKING ASSESSMENT THROUGH COMPETENCY-BASED PRACTICES IN EDUCATION
papers.abstract: Summative grading is traditionally the system of assessment predominantly used in educational institutions worldwide. It typically tests learners’ cognitive, creative, critical, and analytical abilities. However, such examinations often end with the mere demonstration of content knowledge, while competency is lacking. Often, attention is placed on studying for and writing examinations in order to obtain good grade. This creates a significant gap between what learners can reproduce in an exam setting and what they can really do in real-life contexts. This gap highlights the need for competency-based practices and assessments in the education system. Some scholars have discussed competency-based assessment (CBA) as an assessment approach that promotes learning and mastery. It is where learning experience, knowledge and skills are integrated in measuring a learner’s learning ability. This article provides a conceptual analysis of CBA in education, drawing from relevant learning theories and global perspectives to explore its significance in educational practice. It focuses on how CBA promotes active learning by integrating theoretical knowledge with practical skills for application in real-life contexts. Research on global practices showed that many education systems across the world are integrating competency-based practices to enhance learning. The article suggests that CBA practices offer a practical framework for assessing learning within the education system, although it is not without challenges, mainly in measurement and quality of teaching. Despite these challenges, CBA has positive aspects that enhance learning and strengthen the education system. This article recommended, among other things, the combination of summative grading and CBA for effective assessment

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Elemental Distribution Rates in Pyrometallurgical Copper Production
papers.abstract: Understanding elemental distribution among slag, dust, and copper-bearing products during pyrometallurgical copper production is critical for minimizing valuable metal losses, controlling potentially hazardous elements, and improving resource recovery. However, prediction of elemental distribution rates under diverse industrial conditions remains challenging. In this study, multiple machine learning (ML) models were developed and compared for predicting elemental distribution rates based on output-stream descriptors, elemental properties, feed compositions, and process-technology descriptors, using a dataset comprising 370 samples. The ML models were trained and optimized using Bayesian optimization (BO), and permutation importance was used to identify the variables contributing most to the model predictions. The results showed that the optimized CatBoost model achieved the best predictive performance on the independent testing set, with a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.672, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 12.955, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 9.312. Permutation importance analysis indicated that output-stream descriptors mainly provided conditional information for distinguishing prediction scenarios, while elemental descriptors contributed to differentiating element-specific distribution behaviors. Predictions based on constrained virtual samples further revealed distinct element-specific distribution patterns across the five output streams. Zn and Co showed stronger tendencies to report to slag, whereas Hg, As, Bi, and Cd were preferentially enriched in dust; Ni was mainly distributed between converting slag and blister copper. Despite the relatively high importance of elemental properties, no individual elemental descriptor exhibited a consistent monotonic relationship with distribution behavior. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework for predicting elemental distribution rates under heterogeneous industrial conditions, while further improvement in prediction is required for high-precision process control or quantitative mass-balance applications.

papers.title: Dificuldades de aprendizagem no processo de alfabetização: a parceria entre família e escola nos anos iniciais do ensino fundamental
papers.abstract: Early Childhood Education constitutes a fundamental stage of Basic Education, characterized by the centrality of interactions, play, and experiences that foster children's holistic development. In this context, engagement with written language should not be understood merely as a precursor to formal literacy processes, but rather as an opportunity for children to participate in social reading and writing practices. Concurrently, active learning methodologies have gained prominence in educational discourse for valuing student participation, inquiry, collaboration, problem-solving, creative production, and agency. This study aims to analyze, through a bibliographic review, how active learning methodologies can contribute to the development of written language in Early Childhood Education, considering play, games, projects, inquiry, literature, and collective productions as meaningful experiences of engagement with written culture. The study is qualitative and basic in nature, with exploratory and descriptive objectives, conducted through bibliographic research and an integrative literature review. The discussion is grounded in the work of authors such as Vygotsky (2007), Ferreiro and Teberosky (1999), Kishimoto (2011), Soares (2006), Moran (2018), Bacich and Moran (2018), Araujo (2017; 2020), Albuquerque and Ferreira (2020), Sombrio and Pereira (2022), Reis and Amiel (2023), Maia and Dórea (2024), Faria, Silva, and Carvalho (2025), and Paixão and Tassoni (2026), as well as relevant Brazilian regulatory documents. The results of the bibliographic analysis indicate that active learning methodologies can foster meaningful experiences of engagement with written culture when aligned with the characteristics of childhood, playfulness, social interactions, and intentional teacher mediation. It is concluded that the contribution of these methodologies lies not in automatically producing literacy, but in creating contexts in which children can use, explore, interpret, and reinterpret written language in socially meaningful situations.

papers.title: A high-strength, heat-resistant Al-5.7Ni eutectic alloy with a Zr-induced bimodal grain structure fabricated by laser powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: Abstract Eutectic Al–Ni alloys are attractive for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) because their narrow solidification range reduces susceptibility to solidification cracking. In this study, a high-strength, heat-resistant Al–Ni–Zr alloy was fabricated by LPBF using blended Al–5.7Ni and ZrH₂ powders. The composition of the as-built sample is Al–5.72Ni–0.89Zr (wt.%). The alloy exhibited a nanoscale cellular eutectic structure consisting of α-Al cell interiors and Al3Ni-rich cell walls, together with fine equiaxed grains near the melt-pool boundaries and elongated columnar grains within the melt-pool interiors. At room temperature, the alloy achieved a yield strength of 352 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 520 MPa and a fracture elongation of 6.5%. At 300 °C, it retained a yield strength of 165 MPa and an ultimate tensile strength of 188 MPa. The high room-temperature strength is associated with the fine Al3Ni-containing cellular eutectic network, whose largely retained morphology after short-term exposure at 300 °C may also contribute to the elevated-temperature strength. The findings of this study will provide valuable insights for the development of more high-performance LPBF-prepared eutectic aluminum alloys.

papers.title: Teachers' perspectives on physically active learning and student wellbeing in the Nova Scotia Active Smarter Kids Project
papers.abstract: Introduction Active Smarter Kids (ASK) is a Norwegian physically active learning (PAL) program that integrates physical activity into school lessons for students to learn while moving. In 2017, government departments in Nova Scotia (NS), Canada, partnered with ASK to adapt and implement it locally as the NS ASK Project. Since 2018, teachers in over 130 NS schools have been trained in ASK. International studies and a pilot report from NS have noted several benefits of ASK, such as increased physically active time, academic achievement, and executive function. However, a more comprehensive study of the NS ASK project has not been completed. This paper explored elementary and middle school teachers' perceptions of students' wellbeing and the implementation challenges from a PAL project from NS, Canada. Methods Ten teachers (5 elementary, 5 middle school) participated in semi-structured interviews addressing their experience conducting ASK lessons, perceived contributions to students' wellbeing, and any implementation challenges they've encountered. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Seven themes were developed: 1) Fostering belonging and relationship-building; 2) Opportunities for, and experiencing success in, physical activity; 3) The joy of learning with movement; 4) Sharpening engagement and focus; 5) Pedagogical approaches as catalysts for wellbeing; 6) ‘Running' out of resources; and 7) Navigating the status quo. Discussion The project was perceived to support many facets of students' wellbeing through its flexible, adaptable approach, enabling the meeting of different needs and abilities, and positioning it as a promising health-promoting school initiative aligned with global wellbeing frameworks. Implementation challenges, such as a lack of space and curriculum and assessment pressures, can inform efforts to rethink educational systems of similar contexts to remove barriers for PAL.

papers.title: Cost-sensitive active learning for rotating machinery fault diagnosis under data imbalance
papers.abstract: Data-driven fault diagnosis has become an important approach for ensuring the reliability and safety of rotating machinery. However, practical deployment is often hindered by severe data imbalance and label scarcity. Active learning (AL) mitigates label scarcity by selecting the most informative samples for annotation to improve model performance. Nevertheless, conventional AL strategies typically optimize for overall accuracy and treat all misclassifications equally. Consequently, they fail to account for the asymmetric operational costs of diagnostic errors, particularly the greater losses caused by missed detections and severity underestimation. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a cost-sensitive active learning (CS-AL) framework tailored for highly imbalanced fault distributions. In this framework, raw vibration signals are first transformed into two-dimensional time–frequency representations via continuous wavelet transform (CWT). A Bayesian convolutional neural network, integrated with a convolutional block attention module, is developed to extract fault-sensitive features, while epistemic uncertainty is quantified through Monte Carlo (MC) dropout. To explicitly penalize high-risk errors during sample selection, an asymmetric diagnostic cost matrix is constructed to formulate a cost-sensitive acquisition score based on the expected pairwise misclassification cost. To optimize annotation efficiency, a diversity-aware clustering mechanism selects representative prototypes from this high-risk candidate pool. Experimental validations on the CWRU bearing and MCC5-THU gearbox datasets demonstrate that the CS-AL framework achieves enhanced diagnostic performance and significantly reduces high-cost misclassification risks compared to representative AL baselines. The results confirm the effectiveness of CS-AL in accurately allocating limited labeling resources to rare, safety-critical faults while minimizing total operational risk under imbalanced conditions.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning for Skin Cancer Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Skin cancer is one of the most common cancers worldwide. Timely detection substantially improves prognosis, particularly for melanoma. Deep learning models based on convolutional neural networks, Transformers, ensembles, and multimodal learning have advanced automated skin lesion classification and segmentation; however, most remain deterministic and provide no estimate of predictive confidence, which limits their safe use in clinical settings. This systematic literature review examines uncertainty-aware deep learning for skin cancer classification and segmentation across 64 studies published between 2022 and 2026. The reviewed approaches are categorized and compared across Bayesian deep learning, Monte Carlo Dropout, entropy-guided learning, deep ensembles, Transformer-based architectures, explainable artificial intelligence, multimodal learning, federated learning, active learning, and semi-supervised learning, together with quantification techniques such as predictive entropy, mutual information, Expected Calibration Error, conformal prediction, and test-time augmentation. The synthesis shows that although recent models achieve high diagnostic accuracy, uncertainty reporting remains limited, uncertainty thresholds are rarely validated, calibration practices are inconsistent, and external clinical evaluation is scarce. The review maps these gaps to the formulated research questions and outlines future directions toward calibrated, explainable, privacy-preserving, and clinically validated uncertainty-aware dermatological AI systems.

papers.title: Geometric Optimization for Predictive Control of Low-Capacitance CHB-SVGs via Boundary-Chain Search
papers.abstract: Large capacitor-voltage ripple in low-capacitance cascaded H-bridge static var generators (CHB-SVGs) couples current tracking and cluster-voltage balancing. Computing the optimal switching-level solution under the resulting current-band and phase-output constraints requires fast identification of the active constraint faces. This paper proposes a geometric direct model predictive control method for this task. The voltage-balancing objective is rewritten as a weighted distance, converting the constrained optimization into an ellipsoid–polytope first-contact problem. A fast boundary-chain construction and search method is then developed to locate the optimal contact. Auxiliary projections select the relevant constraint faces and guide the construction of boundary chains containing this contact. Weighted-normal criteria direct the search along these chains to identify the active set, from which the optimal switching-level solution is computed. This approach replaces exhaustive active-set enumeration with a directed geometric search while preserving the continuous optimum. Its three-variable phase-level formulation keeps the candidate workload independent of the module count. Simulation and experimental results verify coordinated current tracking and cluster-voltage balancing with the proposed method.

papers.title: DriftGuard: an agentic hybrid temporal transformer and graph attention network framework for autonomous calibration drift detection and correction in distributed marine sensor networks
papers.abstract: Introduction Undetected calibration drift in autonomous ocean sensors corrupts temperature and salinity records underpinning climate reanalysis, seasonal forecasting, and marine ecosystem assessments. With 15–20% of active Argo floats showing meaningful drift at any time and correction workflows taking three to six months, scalable autonomous quality control is urgently needed. Methods We present DriftGuard, a five-component autonomous framework integrating a physically-informed heterogeneous sensor graph over 135 nodes, a Hybrid Temporal Transformer and Graph Attention Network (HybridTGAT), a cross-sensor consistency loss, a conformal prediction wrapper, and a LangGraph-orchestrated three-stage agentic loop supported by a 2,183-chunk RAG store. Results Evaluated on Argo float profiles (116 floats, North Atlantic, 2021–2024), NDBC buoy time series (15 stations, 2019–2024), and the expert-labelled AdapAD benchmark, DriftGuard achieves a GAT-level ROC-AUC of 0.8376, an AdapAD zero-shot AUC of 0.8423, and detects gradual drift types an average of 84.7 readings earlier than the operational Argo QC Test 16 baseline. Operational fleet evaluation across 131 sensors identifies 13 floats in a CRITICAL state requiring correction within 24 hours. Discussion DriftGuard is the first system in the marine sensor domain to unify graph-based spatial reasoning, temporal modelling, autonomous LLM-driven correction, conformal uncertainty certificates, and closed-loop retraining within a single operational pipeline, demonstrating readiness for real-world deployment.

papers.title: SEMINAR: sparsity enhanced mamba with neural iterative regression for predicting unemployment dynamics
papers.abstract: Forecasting unemployment rates using multivariate time series is a tough problem due to its complex temporal dependencies, demographic complexity and need for uncertainty quantification that is interpretable. In labour economics and macro-econometrics, the demographic complexity of the unemployment rate dynamics has been well studied; the recent approaches for deep learning forecasting barely take into account the demographic complexity of the unemployment dynamics. We present SEMINAR: sparsity-enhanced Mamba (SEM), economic priors integration layer (EPIL), adaptive cross-variable attention (ACVA), seasonally-naive anchor-based iterative refinement regression block (IRRB) and probabilistic uncertainty quantifier (PUQ), giving heteroscedastic, horizon-aware confidence intervals. This proposed model is tested against autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), long short-term memory (LSTM), non-sparse Mamba, and transformer in three progressively harder settings using international data for unemployment rate forecasts (2006–2024) in a leak-free chronological protocol with 12-step-ahead multi-horizon forecasting and statistically significant performance evaluation across eight random seeds. In the base setting, SEMINAR gives the best mean absolute error of all five models (128.6 vs . 130.2–149.0 in baselines), beating ARIMA ( p = 0.008) and transformer ( p = 0.039). Under cross-country transfer, SEMINAR is the strongest neural model on the Korea/Chile/Russia task mean absolute error (MAE) (134.6 MAE), although the classical ARIMA baseline remains substantially more accurate there (86.0 MAE); on the short, weakly seasonal Bolivia/Dominican Republic task SEMINAR is outperformed by all four baselines, a failure mode we trace to the seasonal-anchor assumption. Both boundaries are reported rather than omitted. SEMINAR also gives calibrated 80% prediction intervals, a feature that none of the baselines provides in their native form. The complete architecture consists of around 44,401 parameters; an ablation study with seven variants has been done.

papers.title: Energy-Efficient Model Predictive Control of Industrial Induction-Motor Drives: A Systematic Review of Loss-Minimizing, Thermal-Aware, and Data-Driven Strategies
papers.abstract: Induction motors (IMs) consume most of the electricity used in industry, and the efficiency of their drives is classified through the IE and IES classes of IEC 60034-30-1 and IEC 61800-9-2. This PRISMA 2020 systematic review examines energy-efficient model predictive control (MPC) for IM drives using a three-axis taxonomy: efficiency objective (electrical loss, thermal/economic, degradation), solution paradigm (model-based, data-driven, learning-augmented), and uncertainty handling (nominal, observer-based, adaptive/robust). Of the 65 included studies, 43 concern induction-machine drives, but only three of these report an industrial, process, or marine load, and 20 of the 65 address traction or transport. The largest reported effects, 49–65% reductions in drive-cycle loss or energy and light-load efficiency gains of up to about 30 percentage points on a 0.75 kW machine, were obtained in simulation. Hardware-validated IM results mostly amount to about 0.7–4% in efficiency at fixed operating points and 8–18% in drive-cycle energy relative to other MPC variants. These figures are not directly comparable because loss boundaries, operating points, baselines, and validation methods differ. No included study combines a thermal/economic or degradation objective with a data-driven or learning paradigm and adaptive/robust uncertainty handling. Open problems and a research agenda on thermally adaptive economic MPC are outlined.

papers.title: Impact of climate change on malaria incidence in Senegal and Nigeria: a machine learning approach
papers.abstract: Malaria remains a leading climate-sensitive disease in West Africa, where temperature and rainfall variations strongly influence mosquito dynamics and transmission intensity. Senegal and Nigeria, representing the Sahel-Sudanian and rainforest-savanna ecological gradients, are among the most vulnerable zones. However, few climate–malaria forecasting studies combine systematic benchmarking, uncertainty quantification and model explainability within a single framework, or contrast two epidemiologically distinct settings. This study addresses that gap with three objectives: to benchmark a deep recurrent architecture against alternative machine-learning models in two contrasting settings; to quantify predictive uncertainty and validate the framework against independent surveillance data; and to identify the climatic predictors and lags driving the predictions. The BiLSTM implemented here captures the long-term temporal dependencies inherent in climate-driven transmission dynamics. Historical climate data (1985–2014) from the CMIP6 historical experiment were combined with CMIP6 multi-model future projections (2015–2080) under the SSP585 scenario to assess the climatic determinants of malaria incidence. The BiLSTM was calibrated using rainfall and temperature anomalies and benchmarked against six machine-learning models (standard LSTM, GRU, ANN, SVR, Random Forest and Decision Tree), which it matched or exceeded, and externally validated using independent national malaria surveillance data from Senegal and Nigeria. Results show that eastern Senegal experienced a +1.5 °C warming and 20% rainfall decline, while northern Nigeria warmed by +1.2 °C with a 15% rainfall increase. Under SSP585, additional warming of +2–3 °C is projected. The proposed BiLSTM model achieved high predictive accuracy in reproducing the VECTRI-simulated malaria incidence (R 2 between 0.93 and 0.98 across the training, validation and test partitions of both countries). Spatial projections indicate persistent hotspots in southeastern Senegal (Kedougou) and a northward expansion of risk zones in Nigeria by mid-century under SSP585. When the same framework is instead trained and evaluated on observed malaria surveillance data with observed NASA POWER climate in an autoregressive, one-step-ahead setting, it yields a more realistic estimate of operational forecasting skill (test R 2 = 0.72 for Senegal and 0.77 for Nigeria); the near-perfect accuracy obtained against the climate-generated target should therefore be interpreted as an upper bound rather than real-world performance.

papers.title: The Kerboull cross-plate: from the birth of a concept to the current indications
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Reconstruction of major acetabular bone loss remains a demanding challenge during revision total hip arthroplasty. Since its original description, the Kerboull acetabular reinforcement device, also known as the Kerboull cross-plate or cage, has been developed to restore the native hip centre of rotation, to protect bone graft from early mechanical overload, and to allow cementation of a conventional full-polyethylene or a dual mobility cup. METHODS: This narrative review traces the evolution of the Kerboull cross-plate from its original conception to its current indications. RESULTS: We describe the biomechanical rationale of the device, supported by finite-element analyses demonstrating a marked load-sharing effect that protects the underlying bone graft in comparison with other reinforcement devices or unprotected cemented cups. We detail the surgical technique, as originally reported by Kerboull and Hamadouche, together with subsequent refinements aimed at standardising plate positioning. The principles governing graft selection are discussed: segmental structural defects require a structural graft, whereas morselised graft should be reserved for the filling of contained cavitary defects. The biological and mechanical quality of the graft is dependent on its processing, cryopreserved femoral head allograft being preferable to gamma-irradiated allograft. Finally, we review the mid- to long-term outcomes reported with the Kerboull cross-plate, including the more recent trend towards cementing a dual mobility cup within the device to reduce the risk of instability, and we outline the current indications of this technique of reconstruction. CONCLUSION: The Kerboull cross-plate retains its place as a reliable and time-tested option within the modern armamentarium for severe acetabular bone loss reconstruction.

papers.title: From standard to data-driven flow-based design of urban drainage and wastewater management systems: integrating variability, open data, and standardization
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Flowchart showing the transition from conventional to data-driven urban drainage design, supported by four interconnected themes: peak flow variability, open data sources, modelling strategies, and dataset standardization. Urban drainage and wastewater systems face mounting pressures from climate change, urbanization, and evolving regulations. Conventional design approaches based on static standards and conservative safety factors may no longer adequately address the variability, uncertainty, and nonstationarity characterizing current conditions. This review synthesizes Workshop 4 – ‘Influent flowrate generators for system design in urban drainage modelling using open data sources’ – at the 2025 International Conference on Urban Drainage Modelling (UDM2025), examining opportunities to transition toward data-informed, probabilistic models for more accurate flow prediction and system design. Four interconnected themes are explored: (1) accurately representing peak flow variability rather than treating it as noise; (2) the potential of open environmental data sources (satellite observations, global digital elevation models, population datasets) for modelling in data-scarce contexts; (3) the comparative strengths of data-driven, mechanistic, and hybrid modelling approaches, and the conditions governing their appropriate application; and (4) the need for standardized datasets and metadata schemas, drawing lessons from hydrology's CAMELS initiative, to enable reproducible research and large-sample studies. Key conclusions advocate pragmatic hybridization of modelling paradigms, rigorous validation and uncertainty quantification of open data sources, and coordinated international efforts toward a ‘CAMELS for Urban Drainage’ dataset; promising more resilient, efficient, and equitable urban water infrastructure.

papers.title: Multi-indicator Prediction and Multi-Target Model Predictive Control for Coordinated Regulation of NOx Emissions and Ammonia Slip in Cement Kiln Denitrification
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate regulation of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions is essential for stable and environmentally compliant cement production. Cement kiln flue gas denitrification is characterized by strong nonlinearity, long transport delays, multivariable coupling, and uncertain operating disturbances, which make simultaneous NOx control and ammonia-slip suppression difficult. This study proposes a multi-indicator prediction and control framework for cement kiln denitrification. First, a multi-indicator prediction model, named MI-ILTA, is developed by integrating an improved long short-term memory network with a multi-kernel temporal convolutional network and an attention-based feature weighting module. The model is designed for multi-step prediction of NOx concentration and ammonia slip. Based on the predicted outputs, a weighted-sum scalarized Multi-Target Model Predictive Control (MT-MPC) strategy is established to coordinate NOx set-point tracking, ammonia-slip suppression, and smooth ammonia-flow adjustments under process constraints. A differential evolution algorithm solves the rolling optimization problem and determines the control inputs. Industrial data from a cement-plant distributed control system are used to compare the proposed model with TCN, LSTM-TCN, and LSTM-TCN-Attention baselines. The MI-ILTA model achieves lower MAE, RMSE, and SMAPE across the reported prediction horizons for both NOx concentration and ammonia slip. In industrial-data-based closed-loop simulations, the proposed MT-MPC strategy reduces the settling time from 552 s to 366 s and overshoot from 4.1% to 0.38% compared with PID control, while maintaining lower ammonia slip. These results indicate that the proposed framework can improve dynamic regulation and emission stability in cement kiln denitrification systems.

papers.title: A Collaborative Project: Asynchronous Learning Model for Applied Music Pedagogy
papers.abstract: Music students often experience a dip in engagement and progress between weekly music lessons. While digital tools like WhatsApp or email allow for quick communication, they frequently result in fragmented feedback and disorganised archives, hindering consistent progress. This project explored whether asynchronous learning offers unique advantages that make it a valuable, intentional choice for music educators. We asked: How can asynchronous learning aid in applied music pedagogy to develop active learning in voice and piano students? As part of a Masters in Music Leadership (NUS-YST) module, we conducted a four-week collaborative project to examine how asynchronous learning can bridge this gap for both vocal and piano students. We chose Google Classroom as a structured and trackable platform that centralises lesson materials and communication. Within this platform, we adapted specific evidence-based strategies—including spacing and interleaving , Mayer’s 12 multimedia principles , and metacognition —specifically for applied music pedagogy . By applying these principles, such as Mayer’s signalling principle to highlight specific score markings in a video and his segmenting principle to break down complex technical exercises, we fostered student autonomy and helped them engage more critically with their own practice. As a result of this project, we have consolidated a set of practical guidelines (Table1) to support music educators in designing asynchronous lessons that intentionally deepen student autonomy. Attendees will leave with tools to integrate these asynchronous strategies into their own teaching practice to cultivate more independent, 21st-century musicians.

papers.title: Learning Droplet Wetting from Kinetic Theory: Lattice-Boltzmann-Driven Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Rough Surfaces
papers.abstract: Abstract We introduce a lattice Boltzmann-driven Kinetic Physics-Informed Neural Network (K-PINN) for the predictive modeling of droplet dynamics on rough and structured surfaces by embedding the continuous, discrete-velocity Boltzmann–BGK equation, evaluated via automatic differentiation, as the physics-informed learning constraint, with discrete lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) simulations used solely to generate reference training data. Unlike conventional PINNs constrained by macroscopic continuum equations, the proposed framework operates at the mesoscopic kinetic level, preserving the essential physics of the lattice Boltzmann method, including Shan–Chen pseudopotential interactions, within a data-efficient neural framework. Across randomly rough substrates and periodically textured pillar arrays, the K-PINN accurately captures complex interfacial phenomena, including contact line pinning, anisotropic spreading, and capillary hysteresis, while maintaining physical consistency, including mass conservation to within 1.5%. A U-Net-based encoder–decoder architecture achieves a 50–75% reduction in prediction error relative to baseline networks, yielding near-perfect agreement with high-resolution lattice Boltzmann simulations (L2 ≈ 0.021–0.026, R2 ≈ 0.999). Robust convergence across diverse surface morphologies is achieved through curriculum-guided training and adaptive two-stage optimization. Once trained, the model delivers real-time predictions exceeding 104 evaluations per second, offering orders-of-magnitude acceleration over direct numerical simulation and enabling rapid parametric exploration and inverse surface design. By integrating a lattice Boltzmann-based kinetic approach with physics-informed learning, this work presents a mesoscopic physics-informed learning framework for the efficient and accurate prediction of multiphase droplet dynamics.

papers.title: Impact Simulation of Laser Powder Bed-Fused Polymeric Lattice Structures Using Mooney-Rivlin and Yeoh Hyperelastic Material Models: Calibration and Comparison
papers.abstract: This study evaluates a methodology for the calibration of the 5-parameters Mooney-Rivlin and Yeoh 3rd-order hyperelastic material models for impact simulations on laser powder bed-fused TPU1301 lattices destined for personal protective equipment. To calibrate the models, bulk normalized specimens were printed and characterized using 400 mm/min uniaxial compression tests. Three 18% density 20-, 30- and 40 mm-thickness lattice structures, namely, Kelvin, body- and face-centered cubic, were manufactured and impact-tested. Using the material models, the impact tests were simulated using LS-Dyna, and their acceleration curves were compared with their experimental equivalents. The simulations accurately depicted the impact behavior of most lattices, but thicker specimens with lower peak accelerations and longer impact durations, such as the 40 mm Kelvin lattice, showed errors reaching 46 and 64% for the Yeoh and Mooney-Rivlin models, respectively. Furthermore, body-centered cubic lattices showed a softer behavior in simulations than experimentally. Overall, the Yeoh model provided the most accurate results across all topologies with an average error of 11.8% compared with 19.6% for Mooney-Rivlin. The methodology used in this study is therefore considered suitable for LPBF-printed TPU1301 lattice structures but would benefit from calibration at higher strain rates, biaxial and shear testing, and better meshing strategies.

papers.title: MPC Using a Digital Twin Versus Simpler Traditional Heating Control in Swedish Multi-Family Buildings—A Measurement-Based Study
papers.abstract: Our buildings must become more energy efficient. Multi-family buildings account for a significant part of the total energy use. However, many energy-saving measures are very costly and require extensive effort. In this context, improved heating control is a cost-effective supplement. Over the past decade, sensors, machine learning, and related technologies have enabled more advanced heating control. Much of the development relates to model predictive control (MPC), but feedback control (FBC) remains useful on its own and as a stabilising component in various MPC strategies. This field study’s novelty lies in comparing two neighbouring, similar Swedish multi-family buildings with traditional feedforward heating control (FFC). One building was equipped with an established pure FBC strategy and the other with a pure MPC strategy. The latter is based on a tailor-made digital twin with continuous input of real-time weather and household electricity data, etc. In the MPC building, the savings amounted to 11 kWh/m2, and in the FBC building to 6 kWh/m2. The FBC results are consistent with a recent similar field study in the same city. However, the MPC results are unique as they are based on a highly detailed digital twin. The results indicate that, under similar conditions, MPC strategies should involve FBC sparingly if energy efficiency is a high priority.

papers.title: Multiphysics-Guided Neural Networks Integrating Damage Mechanics and Thermodynamic Dissipation for PMMA Plate Impact Analysis Under Pressure Loading
papers.abstract: The impact resistance of thin PMMA plates in deep-sea transparent structures is important for crashworthiness safety and is governed by high-strain-rate loading and hydrostatic pressure. Conventional empirical constitutive models exhibit limited adaptability to strain ratio effects and complex energy dissipation, leading to significant deviations in anti-impact assessment. This study proposes a constitutive-aware physics-informed neural network framework that integrates a data-driven constitutive neural network with embedded physical constraints. Such a proposed constitutive network replaces the theoretical model to capture rate-dependent stress response, while a physics-informed network enforces momentum conservation, energy balance, thermodynamic dissipation inequality, and pressure-induced stress limits. A dynamically weighted multimodal loss function is proposed and is used to ensure stable constraint enforcement during data training. Experimental validation based on a high-speed impact test confirms the constitutive and physics constraint network accuracy. Numerical results demonstrate that increasing hydrostatic pressure alters energy dissipation, increasing residual projectile velocities, and degrading impact resistance. The framework provides an efficient, physically consistent method for evaluating anti-impact performance of thin-walled PMMA structures in deep-sea engineering.

papers.title: Multiscale Digital-Twin Modeling of Energy-Storage Materials by Integrating First-Principles Calculations and Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Conventional modeling of energy-storage materials is constrained by the computational cost of first-principles calculations, limited electrochemical-state awareness in machine-learning interatomic potentials, and weak coupling between materials-scale models and online battery decision-making. This study proposes a first-principles-constrained electrochemically conditioned machine-learning interatomic potential (FP-EMLP) integrated with a multiscale digital-twin framework (FP-EMLP-DT). A multistate configuration space spanning ion concentration, temperature, defects, strain, and phase boundaries is combined with active learning based on committee uncertainty, structural novelty, and physics-based risk. The equivariant graph model incorporates electrochemical-state gating, charge-conserving projection, and differentiable long-range electrostatics, and is trained using energies, forces, stresses, equilibrium voltages, and migration barriers. Predicted diffusion coefficients, free energies, elastic tensors, and chemical expansion coefficients are transferred to an electrochemical-mechanical-thermal-damage model. The resulting model is further integrated with a physics-based reduced-order network, uncertainty-gated residual learning, online data assimilation, and degradation-aware control. FP-EMLP achieves mean absolute errors of 6.5 meV atom−1, 33 meV Å−1, 0.051 V, and 0.038 eV for energy, force, voltage, and migration barrier, respectively, with a 4.8% aggregate relative error across multiscale fields. Active learning reduces required first-principles labels by 33.3% while covering 91.2% of high-risk configurations. FP-EMLP-DT achieves mean absolute errors of 0.93% for state of charge and 1.21% for state of health. papers.abstract: Due to the heterogeneity and uneven distribution of geospatial data, predictive geospatial techniques are often required to provide both accurate target predictions and uncertainty quantification. However, existing approaches typically only provide post-hoc uncertainty estimates, rather than using uncertainty to guide the spatial model training process itself. To address these limitations, we introduce HexaClus++, a supervised, uncertainty-aware, spatial-clustering-based approach that integrates both accuracy and uncertainty to guide local model training on clustered spatial hexagonal regions. To evaluate the performance of our technique, we conduct experiments on property valuation datasets using diverse machine learning approaches. The results demonstrate that HexaClus++, when combined with different base learners, achieves competitive accuracy while also delivering well-calibrated uncertainty, reliable prediction intervals, and enhanced interpretability through regional uncertainty maps and spatially varying feature importance.

papers.title: DIGITAL TWINS FOR HARDWARE-IN-THE-LOOP MODELING OF MOBILE MEDICAL DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS
papers.abstract: The rapid development of mobile medical diagnostic systems, wearable sensors, the Internet of Medical Things, edge computing, and artificial intelligence enables a transition from episodic physiological measurements toward continuous personalized patient monitoring. At the same time, increasing hardware-software complexity requires safe validation of sensing, computing, communication, and diagnostic components before their use with real patients. Hardware-in-the-Loop has already been applied to pacemakers, artificial pancreas systems, automated ventilation, circulatory support, and other medical devices; however, physiological models used in medical HIL environments are typically specialized test models rather than dynamically synchronized digital twins of individual patients. Contemporary Patient Digital Twins increasingly use wearable and IoMT data for personalization, monitoring, and prediction, but they are rarely used as real-time physiological HIL environments for validating physical mobile medical hardware. This paper proposes an integrated Patient Digital Twin–Hardware-in-the-Loop architecture in which a dynamically personalized twin operates in two interconnected modes: as an operational model synchronized with a physical patient for monitoring and diagnosis, and as an executable physiological environment for HIL validation of real sensing, computing, and communication hardware. The architecture integrates a Patient Digital Twin, a Device Digital Twin, mobile/edge processing, synchronization, an HIL interface, diagnostic services, cloud/history services, and a VVUQ layer. The paper formalizes twin state representation, synchronization error, Context-of-Use-dependent fidelity conditions, real-time constraints, and multi-objective mobile model selection. An experimental protocol is proposed to compare software-only simulation, generic physiological HIL, patient-specific static HIL, and dynamically synchronized Patient DT–HIL using fault injection, Verification, Validation and Uncertainty Quantification, diagnostic performance metrics, latency measurements, and energy profiling. The proposed concept provides a methodological basis for reusing one personalized physiological model throughout development, verification, and operation of a mobile medical diagnostic system.

The review synthesizes findings on dynamic visualization tools, which transition mathematics instruction from passive algorithmic drilling to active, condition-based conceptualization. Furthermore, the convergence of traditional deductive reasoning and interactive digital environments is examined through the lens of emerging cognitive vulnerabilities, specifically cognitive overload and superficial engagement. Despite significant methodological maturation, a critical research gap persists regarding the longitudinal validation of how interactive, visual-first learning translates into long-term abstract algebraic fluency. The study concludes that while interactive methods dramatically enhance spatial reasoning and minimize mathematics anxiety, their integration into secondary education relies heavily on the future development of balanced, hybrid pedagogical frameworks that safeguard deep, autonomous computational mastery.

papers.title: Uncertainty quantification in time-lapse full-waveform inversion of vertical seismic profiling data: contrasting the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and Stein Variational Gradient Descent methods
papers.abstract: Abstract Time-lapse full-waveform inversion (TL-FWI) is increasingly important in energy-transition applications, particularly for monitoring CO2 geological storage. Because TL-FWI is highly nonlinear and baseline and monitor surveys commonly differ in acquisition, illumination, and noise conditions, uncertainty quantification is essential for reliable interpretation. Two promising Bayesian approaches are Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) and Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD), which represent the posterior in fundamentally different ways. HMC constructs the posterior through stochastic sampling with gradient-based proposals, whereas SVGD approximates it using a deterministically evolving particle ensemble. Here, we investigate the feasibility of 2D VSP-based TL-FWI using these two approaches under a matched computational budget. Both methods recover the main injection-related velocity anomaly, but they express posterior uncertainty differently. Under this resource-limited comparison, HMC yields uncertainty fields that remain comparatively diffuse and become increasingly difficult to interpret in deeper and off-well regions where illumination is weak. SVGD, in contrast, produces uncertainty patterns that are more strongly organized by acquisition geometry, placing larger uncertainty more explicitly in poorly constrained regions, although this also causes the posterior means and profiles to inherit stronger illumination-shaped artifacts. These results suggest that the practical distinction between HMC and SVGD is not simply one of better or worse uncertainty quantification, but rather how limited computational effort is converted into posterior information. The preferred method is therefore budget- and objective-dependent. Specifically, HMC remains attractive when more exhaustive posterior exploration is computationally feasible, whereas SVGD provides a more scalable and practically interpretable route for rapid uncertainty assessment in TLFWI monitoring applications.

papers.title: Distributed Formation Model Predictive Control Under Communication Denial: An Edge-Splitting ADMM with Centralized-Equivalence Gating and Confidence-Decayed Coupling
papers.abstract: Distributed model predictive control (MPC) coordinates constrained multi-agent systems while preserving computational locality, yet an implementation can cease to represent its stated convex program. We study a minimal linear plant so communication denial is a modeled source of uncertainty, and treat centralized equivalence as a hard gate: an edge-splitting consensus alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) formulation of the formation-tracking quadratic program is built so every distributed update can be audited against a centralized solver. Against a Lagrangian dual-decomposition baseline, ADMM attains the same accuracy without step-size tuning. Across topologies, horizons, penalties, budgets, and denial windows, the exact branch matches the centralized optimum to numerical precision, the equivalence gate and saturation signature survive scaling to eight agents, and the saturation signature also survives measurement noise. For communication denial, we prove a bounded-error result separating the summable-error regime, which recovers the optimum exactly, from the merely-bounded regime, whose limit points remain O(ε)-optimal. Coupling each edge weight to message age through an exponentially decaying confidence factor contracts the distributed problem to uncoupled local MPC, so formation error saturates as outages lengthen; a fixed-weight ablation isolates this decay as the causal mechanism. We contribute a reproducible baseline and two honest mechanisms—centralized-equivalence gating and confidence-decayed coupling—for distributed formation MPC.

papers.title: Promoting active learning and student engagement through critical analysis of scientific illustrations
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Figures and illustrations are central tools for communicating complex biological concepts, yet they necessarily simplify structures and processes, which can obscure important details or introduce misconceptions. This article describes a low-preparation, flexible instructional strategy that leverages these simplifications to promote active learning and student engagement through the critical analysis of scientific illustrations. Instructors prompt students to examine existing figures from textbooks, lectures, or primary literature and identify what is missing, oversimplified, or potentially misleading, as well as how an image could be improved to better represent biological complexity. By modeling this type of analysis and incorporating brief, low-stakes discussions during class, instructors encourage students to view figures as interpretive models rather than complete representations of reality. The approach can be implemented spontaneously, adapted across biological subdisciplines and course levels, and used in lectures or laboratory settings. This strategy shifts students from passive consumption of visuals to active engagement with content, provides opportunities to apply and reinforce conceptual understanding, and provides instructors with real-time insight into student thinking. Overall, using scientific illustrations as prompts for critique provides an accessible strategy to strengthen critical thinking, visual literacy, and understanding of how biological knowledge is communicated.

papers.title: Prediction on tensile mechanical properties of engineered cementitious composites using a fully automated deep learning method
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurately predicting tensile mechanical properties of Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC), including tensile strength (TS) and ultimate tensile strain (UTS), remains challenging, particularly for the ultimate tensile strain, which exhibits high data dispersion that hinders reliable predictions. While machine learning (ML) has shown significant promise in predicting the mechanical properties of ECC, it faces several challenges: (1) limited predictive accuracy; (2) complexity and time-consuming nature of hyperparameter tuning; (3) insufficient research into predicting the UTS of ECC. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a fully automated deep learning model enhanced by Bayesian optimization for predicting the tensile mechanical properties of polyethylene fiber-reinforced engineered cementitious composites (PE-ECC). First, convolutional neural network (CNN) model was employed to enhance feature extraction and predictive accuracy. Second, Bayesian optimization was utilized to automatically construct the network and optimize various hyperparameters, resulting in an optimized network. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed Bayesian-optimized convolutional neural network (BO-CNN) method in predicting PE-ECC's TS and UTS, utilizing a dataset of 154 experimental samples from published literature, achieving coefficients of determination () of 0.911 and 0.775, respectively. The BO-CNN method not only outperforms CNNs and artificial neural networks (ANNs) optimized through grid search but also surpasses other eleven traditional ML models. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was employed to interpret input features' contributions in the prediction of tensile mechanical properties. Overall, the proposed method provides an efficient and reliable solution for predicting the tensile mechanical properties of ECC.

papers.title: SYSTEM-FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS OF COMPLEX PRODUCTS FOR DIGITAL TWIN AND HIL MODEL DEVELOPMENT
papers.abstract: Modern complex engineering products are multi-level cyber-physical systems in which mechanical, electrical, sensing, computing, communication, control, actuator and energy components operate as a tightly interconnected whole. Consequently, the adequacy of a Digital Twin or Hardware-in-the-Loop model depends not only on the accuracy of individual component models but also on the correct representation of subsystem interactions. The purpose of this study is to develop a system-functional approach for identifying critical inter-subsystem dependencies that have to be represented when constructing Digital Twin and HIL models of complex products. Current approaches based on Model-Based Systems Engineering, Digital Twins, Functional Mock-up Interface, co-simulation, Hardware-in-the-Loop and Verification, Validation and Uncertainty Quantification are analysed. A decomposition of a complex mobile computer system into physical, sensing, computing, software, communication, control, actuator, energy, human-machine and environmental subsystems is proposed. Physical, informational, control, temporal, energy and uncertainty-related dependencies are classified. The system is formalised as a multilayer directed graph, while subsystem interfaces are described using signal values, update frequencies, latency, jitter, bandwidth and uncertainty characteristics. A dependency criticality assessment method combining system-functional significance, global sensitivity, HIL ablation effects and real-time execution impact is proposed. The construction of a minimally sufficient DT–HIL model is formulated as a multi-criteria optimisation problem in which computational complexity is minimised subject to accuracy, stability and real-time constraints.

papers.title: Topology-Constrained Saddle-Point Reconstruction of Strong-Field Photoelectron Momentum Spectra
papers.abstract: In strong-field ionization, complex-time saddle points are closely related to electron emission times and quantum-orbit interference patterns. However, not all solutions to the saddle-point equation carry physical contributions. Saddle coalescence can also invalidate the isolated-saddle approximation. Within the strong-field-approximation framework, we propose a topology-constrained approach to reconstruct photoelectron momentum spectra. A physics-informed neural network is employed to produce candidate roots, which are subsequently refined via a Newton-type iteration. A topological selector is defined by the non-zero support of intersection numbers to filter unphysical solutions, while local coherent continuation for pole-saddle pairs handles saddle-coalescence regions. We test our method on hydrogen atoms subjected to six-cycle elliptically polarized laser fields and compare the reconstructed spectra with direct numerical strong-field-approximation results. For 300 nm and 500 nm driving fields, the normalized relative L2 errors on the linear probability scale reach 3.793% and 3.520%, respectively. Our method improves the physical interpretability of saddle-based spectrum reconstruction within the strong-field approximation and is promising for other problems in computational physics involving saddle-point equations.

papers.title: Smart Energy Management of Hybrid EV–Hydrogen Stations Through LSTM Forecasting and Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and hydrogen-powered vehicles requires integrated energy infrastructures capable of simultaneously addressing electricity and hydrogen demands while accommodating the variability of renewable energy sources. This study evaluates the operational performance of a renewable-powered hybrid EV charging and hydrogen refueling station through predictive energy management. The station integrates photovoltaic and wind generation, grid connection, an electrolyzer, hydrogen storage, and vehicle charging/refueling infrastructure. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model was employed to jointly forecast renewable generation, EV charging demand, and hydrogen demand using a 24-h historical window and a 10-h prediction horizon. These forecasts were incorporated into a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework to coordinate coupled electricity–hydrogen energy flows and were comparatively evaluated against a rule-based energy management system (RB-EMS) under the same operating conditions. Aggregate forecasting performance was evaluated using MAE, RMSE, and R2 metrics. Compared with RB-EMS, LSTM–MPC reduced total grid energy consumption by 10.6% and peak grid demand by 20.8%, while providing a modest increase in hydrogen demand served. The results indicate that forecast-assisted predictive management can improve grid-side performance and support coordinated operation of renewable-powered EV–H2 infrastructures.
