papers.abstract: Background: Case-Based Learning (CBL) is a student-centered teaching method that promotes active learning, critical thinking, and clinical reasoning.This study compared the effectiveness of CBL and Traditional Lecture-Based Teaching in enhancing learning outcomes in Physiology among first-year MBBS students.Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional comparative study was conducted among 240 first-year MBBS students in the Department of Physiology at S V Medical College.Students were divided into two groups of 120 each by simple randomization.Group A was taught using CBL, while Group B received Traditional Lecture-Based Teaching on the topic jaundice.Pre-test and post-test assessments consisting of MCQs and SAQs were conducted.Statistical analysis was performed using paired t-test and independent t-test.Results: Both groups showed significant improvement in post-test scores.In the CBL group, MCQ scores improved from 16.93 ± 2.21 to 19.51 ± 1.10 (p < 0.001), and SAQ scores improved from 7.04 ± 2.53 to 13.56 ± 2.32 (p < 0.001).In the traditional teaching group, MCQ scores improved from 17.31 ± 2.26 to 18.49 ± 1.91 (p < 0.05), while SAQ scores improved from 6.58 ± 2.48 to 10.46 ± 2.50 (p < 0.002).Greater improvement was observed in the CBL group.Conclusion: CBL was found to be more effective than traditional lecture-based teaching in improving comprehension, reasoning ability, and retention of knowledge among first-year MBBS students.

papers.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Dentistry: Promise, Pitfalls, and Evidence Gaps.
papers.abstract: GLP-1RAs (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists) have become one of the fastest-growing drug classes worldwide, with prescriptions for obesity treatment increasing by 587% from 2019 to 2024. While their metabolic and cardiovascular benefits are well established, the implications for oral health remain largely unexamined. Preclinical evidence consistently demonstrates anti-inflammatory and osteoprotective effects on periodontal and peri-implant tissues: GLP-1RAs promote osteogenic differentiation of periodontal ligament stem cells, reduce alveolar bone resorption in animal models of periodontitis, and enhance implant osseointegration in diabetic rats. However, these findings are based exclusively on in vitro and animal studies, with only a single retrospective cohort study providing limited clinical data. Conversely, several oral adverse effects have been reported based on pharmacovigilance analyses, including xerostomia, dysgeusia, and anosmia, particularly for semaglutide. Gastrointestinal side effects, particularly nausea (15% to 50%), vomiting (5% to 24%), and gastroesophageal reflux, pose a plausible but unquantified risk for tooth erosion and secondary caries. A bidirectional link between GLP-1 signaling and the oral microbiota, mediated by bacterial dipeptidyl peptidase (DPP)-4-like enzymes that degrade endogenous GLP-1, adds further complexity. Despite this breadth of potential interactions, no prospective study has used any dental outcome as an endpoint in patients receiving GLP-1RAs. This critical appraisal synthesizes the evidence across multiple dental disciplines, grades it in each domain, and identifies the gaps that demand urgent investigation.

papers.title: Matched-Capacity Comparison of Additive and Multiplicative Neural Network Surrogates for Response Prediction of Steel Roof Trusses
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Repeated finite element analyses account for most of the computational effort in designing steel roof trusses, and neural network surrogates can remove much of this burden. However, the influence of the neuron model on surrogate quality is seldom examined under controlled conditions. In this work, an additive multilayer perceptron (MLP) and a multiplicative neuron model (MNM) of nearly equal size (211 and 196 trainable parameters, respectively) are compared. Training data were drawn from a parametric STAAD.Pro database of 46,140 Fink, Howe, Pratt and Warren trusses checked against IS 800:2007, in which non-compliant designs were deliberately retained. Using nineteen input variables, each network estimated eight continuous responses together with a binary pass/fail design status. On held-out test data, the mean coefficient of determination of the MLP ranged from 0.942 to 0.946 across the four profiles, compared with 0.700 to 0.775 for the MNM. The corresponding mean absolute percentage errors were 11–17 % and 26–37 %. Total weight was the most accurately estimated response (MLP R² ≥ 0.964), while the maximum utilisation ratio was the least accurate (R² ≈ 0.80–0.83), because the critical member shifts from one region of the design space to another. In pass/fail classification, the false negative rate of the MLP was 0.074–0.213, against 0.210–0.608 for the MNM. Since the MNM used a bounded geometric-mean aggregation and had marginally fewer parameters, its weaker performance is traced to the multiplicative form itself, which is poorly suited to the largely additive behaviour of truss responses. The MLP is therefore recommended as the surrogate, with its utilisation predictions regarded as the least reliable output. Key words: neural network surrogate, steel roof truss, multiplicative neuron model, multilayer perceptron, IS 800:2007, STAAD.Pro.

papers.title: Tissue-engineered constructs based on biodegradable scaffolds: history, current state and prospects of clinical application
papers.abstract: Tissue engineering is one of the areas of regenerative medicine focused on the design and development of tissue-engineered constructs (TECs) capable of restoring, replacing, or supporting the function of damaged tissues. Biodegradable scaffolds — biomimetic analogues of the extracellular matrix that provide spatial organization of cells and modulate cellular behavior — constitute a key component of most TECs. This review examines the historical foundations of tissue engineering and the evolving concepts behind TECs. Biodegradable scaffolds are considered the principal platform for the majority of current tissue engineering approaches and a critical determinant of their future clinical translation. We summarize data on scaffold materials, forms, and fabrication technologies, including decellularization, electrospinning, cryostructuring, 3Dprinting, and bioprinting, and outline the design requirements for TECs according to the target tissue. Methods for physicochemical and biological evaluation of TECs in vitro and in vivo are reviewed, together with challenges related to standardization of assessment protocols. Using cartilage, liver, and pancreas TECs as examples, we illustrate the capabilities and limitations of contemporary tissue engineering strategies. Major barriers to clinical translation are analyzed, including vascularization, immune-inflammatory responses, selection of cell sources, the need for scalable manufacturing, and regulatory considerations. Emerging directions in the field are discussed, such as personalized constructs, prevascularization strategies, 3D bioprinting, and integration with gene-based approaches. The aim of this review is to examine the evolution, current status, and clinical prospects of TECs based on biodegradable scaffolds.

papers.title: The association between body mass index and perioperative outcomes by ethnicity and socioeconomic status: a systematic review of systematic reviews
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Body mass index (BMI) is associated with adverse perioperative outcomes. This study investigated the completeness of ethnicity and socioeconomic status (SES) reporting in perioperative research and the association between BMI and perioperative outcomes by ethnicity and SES. DESIGN: We extended a previous systematic review of reviews that compared perioperative outcomes by BMI categories. For this review, we extracted primary studies published from 2004 onwards from included systematic reviews that focused on seven frequently performed surgeries with some evidence of ethnic disparities: total hip arthroplasty, total knee arthroplasty, coronary artery bypass grafting, caesarean section, prostatectomy, breast reconstruction postmastectomy, and gynaecological surgery. We calculated the number (%) of primary studies reporting ethnicity and/or SES and extracted data for perioperative outcomes up to 90 days postoperatively by ethnicity and SES. Outcomes were based on the Standardised Endpoints in Perioperative Medicine initiative. Effect measures and incidence (%) were qualitatively summarised due to heterogeneity in reporting. RESULTS: From 49 systematic reviews, 332 primary studies investigated the seven surgical procedures and only 39 (11.7%) reported ethnicity (10.8%) or SES (2.4%) at baseline. Among these, only 10 studies (3%) stratified perioperative outcomes by ethnicity and/or SES, with most adjusting for BMI in regression models. Only one study clearly stratified outcomes across BMI categories within each ethnicity. There was some evidence of increasing risk of postoperative atrial fibrillation by ethnicity and BMI. Two studies found that Black patients had higher odds of pulmonary embolism than White patients after adjusting for BMI. Findings for other outcomes and SES were inconsistent. CONCLUSION: Poor reporting of ethnicity and SES data limits understanding of how these variables modify the association between BMI and perioperative outcomes. Deliberate inclusion of ethnicity and SES data in study design, analysis, and reporting is needed to address inequality in perioperative research.

papers.title: Digital twin-driven surrogate optimization for maximum power point tracking of photovoltaic systems under partial shading conditions
papers.abstract: Photovoltaic systems under partial shading develop multimodal power-voltage characteristics that render conventional gradient-based MPPT algorithms ineffective. Bio-inspired metaheuristic approaches overcome local-maxima entrapment but introduce a structural scan-phase energy loss: each search iteration physically evaluates a candidate duty cycle on the PV hardware, dissipating real energy at every shading event. This paper presents the Digital Twin-Driven Surrogate-Optimized MPPT (DTSO-MPPT) model, which substantially reduces hardware scan losses by decoupling the global search from the physical PV system and limiting hardware interaction to VTC-based verification. The proposed four layer architecture has a physics calibrated Digital Twin with Recursive Least Squares, a surrogate PV surface builder to evaluate the calibrated model, an Orangutan Optimization algorithm to search the surrogate for the global optimum and finally a validation and transfer controller to verify the accuracy conditions. The proposed model was implemented and numerically evaluated in MATLAB R2024b/Simulink 24.1 under five partial-shading conditions. The simulation results exhibit the proposed model tracking efficiency as 99.1%, GMPP convergence in 0.14s, steady-state power oscillation averaging approximately 0.53 W and remaining within 0.42–0.58 W across the five evaluated cases. The scan-loss reduction energy efficiency metric of 99.4% obtained by the proposed quantifies the reduction in scan-loss, which represents the principal advantage over conventional hardware-coupled MPPT methods.

papers.title: Diagnostic performance of perioperative inflammatory and coagulation biomarkers for periprosthetic joint infection
papers.abstract: Distinguishing periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) from aseptic failure remains challenging, as both conditions may present with systemic inflammatory changes. Although C-reactive protein (CRP) and other conventional inflammatory markers are widely used, their diagnostic performance is not always sufficient. This study aimed to evaluate whether available preoperative biomarkers reflecting systemic inflammation and coagulation could improve the identification of PJI in patients undergoing revision total hip arthroplasty (THA) or total knee arthroplasty (TKA). We retrospectively reviewed 379 patients who underwent revision total hip or knee arthroplasty between December 2019 and December 2024, including 172 patients with PJI and 207 with aseptic revision group. The last available preoperative laboratory results before revision surgery were analyzed, including hematological inflammatory indices, including neutrophil–lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), albumin-globulin ratio, interleukin-6 (IL-6), C-reactive protein (CRP), D-dimer, and fibrinogen (Fib). Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to assess diagnostic performance. Univariate logistic regression analyses were used to assess the associations between individual biomarkers and PJI, followed by an exploratory multivariable logistic regression model adjusted for gender. A nomogram was developed from this exploratory model and evaluated using calibration analysis and decision curve analysis (DCA). Among the evaluated biomarkers, SII showed good overall discrimination for distinguishing PJI from aseptic revision, with an area under the curve of 0.830. At the Youden-derived cutoff of 768.125, SII had a sensitivity of 56.6% and a specificity of 92.8%. When dichotomized at the Youden-derived cutoffs, elevated SII (> 768.125; OR 12.526; 95% CI 6.599–25.962) and CRP (> 6.840 mg/L; OR 7.942; 95% CI 4.664–14.075) were both associated with PJI (both P < 0.001). In an exploratory model adjusted for gender, SII (aOR, 9.751; 95% CI 4.905–20.988; p < 0.001) and CRP (aOR, 6.205; 95% CI 3.449–11.556; p < 0.001) remained associated with PJI. The nomogram incorporating SII, CRP, and gender achieved an apparent AUC/C-index of 0.867 (95% CI 0.818–0.917) and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.865 after 1000 bootstrap resamples. The optimism-corrected calibration slope was 0.954, with a Brier score of 0.151. SII showed good discriminative ability for distinguishing PJI revision from aseptic revision. However, its limited sensitivity at the selected cutoff precludes its use as a standalone screening or rule-out test. SII should therefore be interpreted as an adjunctive marker together with established diagnostic findings. The nomogram incorporating SII, CRP, and gender demonstrated promising apparent performance after internal validation. The underlying revision-arthroplasty biomarker cohort was retrospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on April 26, 2022 (ChiCTR2200059185), after data collection had begun. papers.title: Intelligent MPPT in PV Systems using metaheuristic-optimised deep neural networks
papers.abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems face problems with multiple local maxima, poor tracking efficiencies and unstable maximum power point tracking (MPPT) when the irradiance changes rapidly or when there is partial shading on the panels. Traditional MPPT methods including Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductance display slow convergence and oscillation around the steady state in the changing environment. This paper proposes a Digital Twin-based Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO-Deep Neural Network) intelligent MPPT system for solar PV systems to overcome these two issues.This paper proposes a hybrid Grey wolf optimization –Deep neural Network (GWO_DNN) based MPPT technique for photovoltaic systems. The comparison between hybrid deep neural network (DNN)-based controllers for maximally tracking MPPs through Grey Wolf Optimisation (GWO), Golden Eagle Optimisation (GO) and Moth-Flame Algorithm (MFA) are evaluated by comparing relative effectiveness based upon converging performance, prediction accuracy, computational efficiency and stability. The proposed method improves tracking efficiency, reduces steady-state oscillations and achieves faster convergence under varying irradiance conditions. Computational models show GWO-DNN controllers achieving lower test mean absolute distance from the true MPP compared to the other controllers with mean absolute mean square errors (MAE) reported as 0.6138 V (GWO-DNN), 0.3506 V (MFA-DNN) and 0.4978 V (GO-DNN). The GWO-DNN controllers also have a lower degree of oscillation in steady-state conditions, showing faster convergence than all other controllers as well as significantly lower prediction errors. In contrast, Moses-DNN performs more reliably with respect to optimal positioning, but its predictive capabilities will limit its effectiveness for practical real-time implementation. Although GO-DNN provides lower inference time than both the GWO app and MFA model as is a whole, the standard deviation of how far down the MPP would be estimated will increase for the time taken to make the prediction. A traditional CNN-LSTM model has demonstrated to consistently underperform under dynamic operating conditions. Thus, the results demonstrate that GWO-DNN represents a superior balance of MPPT controller characteristics across dynamic operating ranges, as such, GWO-DNN will provide the most robust and predictable MPP capability for use in smart solar energy applications. This initiative helps meet the UN Sustainable Development Goals through the past improvements made in renewable energy extraction efficiency, the creation of more intelligent energy infrastructure and ultimately the contribution to greater levels of solar energy production, while also reducing wasted energy through better designs. Specifically, it contributes to SDG7 - Affordable and Clean Energy; SDG9 - Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure; and SDG13 - Climate Action by facilitating the creation of sustainable, resilient and low-carbon energy systems.

papers.title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN AUTOMATION AND INTELLIGENT CONTROL SYSTEM FOR THE DRYING PROCESS OF POLYVINYL CHLORIDE
papers.abstract: This study develops a structured automation and intelligent control concept for suspension-grade polyvinyl chloride (S-PVC) drying. The proposed architecture combines industrial instrumentation, a model-assisted outlet-moisture soft sensor, online bias adaptation, and constrained model predictive control (MPC). A control-oriented drying model represents moisture removal by an effective rate coefficient and first-order outlet dynamics with transport delay. A reproducible four-hour numerical experiment compares a conventional PI controller with the bias-adaptive MPC under stepwise variations in wet-cake moisture. For the explicitly assumed nominal parameters, MPC reduced the calculated mean utility-demand proxy from 303.19 to 300.31 kW (0.95%) and reduced the proportion of simulated time above the illustrative 0.43% dry-basis moisture limit from 20.4% to 0.0%. A ±10% kinetic-parameter sensitivity test showed both the value and the limitations of online model correction. These are model-based findings, not results of industrial commissioning or laboratory validation. The paper specifies an implementation and validation route for production-scale deployment.

papers.title: A hybrid scale attention network for uncertainty aware brain tumor MRI classification
papers.abstract: Accurate and reliable classification of brain tumors from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is critical for timely clinical decision-making. Existing deep learning methods suffer from three key limitations: overconfident predictions without principled uncertainty estimates, lack of external validation across acquisition protocols, and parameter-heavy architectures unsuitable for resource-constrained deployment. To address these gaps, we propose Hybrid Scale-Attention Network, a lightweight framework comprising an EfficientNet-B3 backbone, a depthwise-separable Adaptive Multi-Scale Module (AMSM), and an Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) classification head. AMSM fuses three parallel dilated convolutional branches at rates {1, 2, 4} and an identity branch via learned softmax gating, forming a convex combination of multi-scale representations at an approximately 6.6× lower parameter cost than equivalent standard convolutions. The EDL head enables single-pass evidential uncertainty estimation based on Dirichlet strength. Through systematic four-variant ablation, we find that stacking a Dual Attention Module after AMSM degrades cross-dataset generalization despite modest in-domain gains, motivating its exclusion. On BRISC 2025, the proposed model achieves 99.20% accuracy and 99.30% macro-F1 with only 10.97 M parameters. Development-stage external validation on the PMRAM-BD cohort yields 97.41% accuracy without fine-tuning, indicating strong cross-dataset performance. Misclassified samples carry higher mean evidential uncertainty than correctly classified ones, with a misclassification detection AUROC of 0.9461 at single-pass inference cost (16.8 ms), offering an efficient alternative to MC-Dropout. Grad-CAM and UA-GradCAM visualizations alongside MSAD provide radiologist-interpretable localization and per-class scale-branch analysis. These results demonstrate that the proposed model offers a favorable trade-off among accuracy, parameter efficiency, and principled uncertainty quantification, supporting potential retrospective clinical investigation.

papers.title: A generalized parameter calibration framework for typhoon wave models using pre-optimization dimensionality reduction in the South China Sea
papers.abstract: Accurate simulation of wave fields under extreme typhoon sea states is of great significance to ocean engineering and disaster prevention and mitigation. However, third-generation wave models still exhibit considerable uncertainty under strong wind conditions, and their empirical parameters lack systematic calibration. Targeting the South China Sea (SCS) as the study area, this paper proposes an automated parameter calibration framework based on “Morris global sensitivity analysis and Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization” utilizing the ST6 source term package of the WAVEWATCH III (WW3) model. First, a sensitivity analysis is conducted on nine key physical parameters, identifying CDFAC, SINWS, SINA0, SWLB1, and GAMMA as the dominant parameters. Subsequently, aimed at multi-typhoon joint calibration (Kompasu, Maon), an objective function is constructed based on the mean root mean square error (RMSE) from 10 typhoon buoy samples, and 200 optimization iterations are performed. The results indicate that the optimal parameter combination reduces the mean RMSE of the calibration set from 0.5167 m to 0.3800 m, an improvement of 26.5%, yielding a parameter combination significantly superior to the default configuration for the SCS. Validated by four independent typhoons (Nesat, Mangkhut, Molave, Saudel) involving 17 typhoon buoy samples, the independent validation set showed an improvement of 29.69% in the mean RMSE and an approximately 61.86% reduction in the mean absolute Bias, which verifies its robustness and generalization capability. This study provides an efficient and transferable parameter calibration method, and the obtained optimal parameters demonstrate excellent applicability for typhoon wave simulations in the SCS.

papers.title: System-level seismic fragility prediction of high-speed railway track-bridge system based on deep learning
papers.abstract: Rapid post-earthquake assessment of high-speed railway track–bridge systems (HSRTBS) is essential for restoring service and managing seismic risk. Conventional nonlinear time-history analysis (NTHA) is the standard tool for response estimation, but its high computational cost in multi-component systems makes it impractical for rapid use. To address this gap, this paper proposes a deep learning (DL) framework that predicts the seismic response and fragility of HSRTBS directly from ground-motion (GM) records. The core of the framework is the CNN–ResNet–LSTM (C-R-L) model, which takes GM time histories as input and outputs both the response time histories and the peak responses for multiple components. A Bayesian optimization (BO) algorithm tunes the key hyperparameters to improve generalization, and ablation studies quantify the contribution of each module. The trained model predicts component-level seismic responses with high accuracy: the coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) for time-history prediction reaches 0.966, and peak-response errors are mostly between 2% and 12%. Embedded in the fragility analysis pipeline, the model further reproduces the system-level fragility curves of HSRTBS. The predicted curves agree closely with those from conventional analysis, with R 2 values above 0.95 in most cases and an average error of within 5%. The proposed framework therefore preserves predictive accuracy while substantially reducing the time burden of repeated NTHA, providing a practical route to rapid post-earthquake damage and system-risk assessment of HSRTBS.

papers.title: Plug-and-play predictive energy management for fuel-efficient platooning of gasoline-powered autonomous vehicles
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a plug-and-play predictive energy management framework for fuel-efficient platooning of gasoline-powered autonomous vehicles. Unlike existing approaches that target electric or hybrid drivetrains, the proposed architecture addresses the nonlinear thermodynamic and aerodynamic challenges inherent to internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles. The framework integrates an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System optimized via Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (ANFIS-TLBO) with Model Predictive Control (MPC) and a Quantum-inspired Long Short-Term Memory (QLSTM) network that broadcasts a 10-second leader state prediction horizon to all follower vehicles simultaneously. A cooperative power-sharing mechanism and a predictive gap policy are superimposed as a lightweight supervisory layer that leaves the internal structure and parameters of each local controller entirely unchanged, modifying only its reference inputs (predicted leader trajectory, desired gap, and coordinated fuel-cut activation). The framework is validated across four standardized driving cycles, HWFET, US06, Artemis HW130, and Artemis HW150, in both 4-vehicle and 6-vehicle homogeneous platoon configurations, each subjected to 20 statistically independent runs incorporating stochastic wind (Weibull) and road grade (Rayleigh) disturbances. Under the HWFET cycle, the proposed method achieves an average per-vehicle fuel consumption of 6.64 L/100 km (4-vehicle platoon) and 6.61 L/100 km (6-vehicle platoon), outperforming all benchmarks including Adaptive MAB, Pure ANFIS, Pure MPC, and Pure TLBO. NOx emission reduction rates from leader to last follower reach 5.74% and 6.23% in the respective configurations, the highest recorded across all methods, reflecting a trade-off in which the leader operates at a higher absolute NOx level to sustain tighter velocity tracking, while followers benefit disproportionately from predictive power management. The plug-and-play architecture is validated on a 6-vehicle platoon with zero controller retuning, confirming scalability across platoon sizes without local-controller modification.

papers.title: A generalizable supervised operator learning framework based on Kolmogorov–Arnold networks for structured grid generation with boundary control
papers.abstract: Mesh quality is paramount for the accuracy of numerical simulations. Structured grids are favored in engineering for their superior discretization, yet their generation faces an inherent trade-off between quality and efficiency. Physics-informed neural network approaches rapidly generate high-quality meshes, yet they are constrained by limited generalizability, requiring retraining for varying geometry inputs. In this paper, we propose a model termed MKoNet, a generalizable supervised operator learning framework for structured grid generation with boundary control. The model utilizes operator learning to directly capture the underlying physical laws governing the partial differential equations (PDEs), thereby generating high-quality meshes for varying geometric boundaries without the need for retraining. Specifically, our loss function incorporates a dedicated boundary-control term, which alleviates the severe element distortion near boundaries observed in existing methods and improves mesh quality. Furthermore, we replace traditional multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) with Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KANs), achieving enhanced model performance with a substantially reduced parameter count. Experimental results across diverse geometric configurations demonstrate that MKoNet can generate high-quality structured grids with effective boundary control and strong robustness. The proposed method achieves competitive or superior performance across most evaluated metrics, particularly for challenging geometries with complex boundaries.

papers.title: Investigation on melting characteristics, mechanical properties and microstructure of Ta-W alloy fabricated via LPBF
papers.abstract: Ta-W refractory alloys have attracted increasing attention for extreme applications owing to the excellent high-temperature performance. Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) overcomes the challenges of manufacturing complex Ta-W structures. However, the high melting point and limited laser absorption hinder stable forming during LPBF processing. This paper investigated the effects of laser power and scanning speed on melt-pool morphology, two-phase region and track stability based on single-track melting and printing, and a stable single-track processing window of 200-250 W and 400-500 mm/s was identified. The forming behavior of the Ta-5W alloys was further evaluated based on volume energy density (VED), although similar VED values resulting from different power-velocity combinations produced different defect morphologies. Microstructural observations indicated that cooling variations caused by scanning speed affect grain morphology, while variations in recrystallization behavior induced by laser power resulted in local residual stresses. The Ta-5W alloy fabricated under optimized parameters of 250 W and 500 mm/s achieved a tensile strength of 667.3 MPa and an elongation of 20.51%. This study provides a process window and analytical foundation for the fabrication of Ta-W refractory alloys using LPBF.

papers.title: A hybrid predictive and uncertainty-aware framework for renewable hydrogen system efficiency assessment and sustainable energy planning
papers.abstract: Abstract Renewable hydrogen is emerging as a critical element in the transition toward low-carbon and sustainable energy systems; however, accurately evaluating system efficiency remains challenging due to complex, nonlinear interactions among technical and environmental factors. This study proposes a hybrid predictive and uncertainty-aware framework for assessing renewable hydrogen system efficiency and supporting sustainable energy planning. The framework integrates Elastic Net and Extra Trees regression models enhanced through meta-heuristic optimization using Sparrow Search and Firefly algorithms to improve predictive performance. Recursive Feature Elimination is applied to identify the most influential variables governing system behavior, while Dempster–Shafer Theory is incorporated to model uncertainty and construct a robust ensemble prediction strategy. The proposed approach is evaluated using a dataset of 2,535 renewable hydrogen system records with spatial attributes derived from documented geographical coordinates. Experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in predictive accuracy, with a 12% increase in R² and a 15% reduction in MAE compared to baseline approaches. Sensitivity analysis indicates that photovoltaic power generation and electrolysis efficiency are the most influential factors affecting hydrogen system performance. Beyond improved prediction accuracy, the framework provides interpretable insights that can support infrastructure development, investment planning, and energy policy design. The proposed methodology demonstrates how hybrid predictive modeling combined with uncertainty quantification can enhance decision-making processes in renewable hydrogen systems and contribute to more reliable low-carbon energy transitions.

papers.title: Rapid 2D Occam’s Inversion of Ultra-Deep Borehole Azimuthal Resistivity Measurements
papers.abstract: Summary A rapid two-dimensional (2D) Occam’s inversion method is developed to interpret ultra-deep borehole azimuthal resistivity (UDAR) measurements acquired in complex dipping formations and along arbitrary well trajectories. While conventional one-dimensional (1D) inversion approaches are computationally efficient, they are inadequate to capture lateral variations of electrical resistivity and structural complexity, hence limiting their accuracy and reliability in realistic geological settings. The developed method extends the inversion into both 2D longitudinal and 2D transverse directions with respect to the well trajectory, providing greater accuracy of inversion results than possible with 1D inversion while maintaining computational efficiency. A new regularization scheme is incorporated into the 2D Occam’s inversion formulation to enforce consistency of the inversion model with the local geological orientation. In contrast to traditional Tikhonov regularization, which often yields overly smooth models, this scheme utilizes 2D Total Variation (TV) model weighting matrices to estimate sharper layer boundaries and reduce structural artefacts. The Jacobian matrix is efficiently computed and updated using a new Block Gauss–Radau modelling algorithm via the adjoint method, which provides improved accuracy, faster convergence, and greater stability compared to the traditional Spectral Lanczos Decomposition Method (SLDM). To overcome the non-uniqueness of inversion, a logit transformation is applied to constrain the inverted model properties within realistic physical limits. Anderson acceleration is incorporated to further enhance convergence speed and stability of the nonlinear inversion process. Lastly, a new uncertainty quantification approach based on Bayesian extrapolation is integrated into the inversion that captures the spatial sensitivity of the measurements to the spatial distribution of electrical resistivity. The method is validated on synthetic and field data, verifying improved performance over 1D inversion results through reduced artefacts, lower data misfit, and decreased model uncertainty, while producing results within minutes for efficient real-time well-geosteering applications.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning for sustainable polymeric marine antifouling coatings: current evidence, challenges, and future perspectives
papers.abstract: Marine biofouling causes significant economic and environmental impacts by increasing drag, fuel consumption, emissions, maintenance costs, and material degradation. Despite advances in sustainable antifouling coatings, their development still relies largely on trial-and-error approaches. Recent advances in AI, ML, and materials informatics can accelerate the discovery and optimization of sustainable marine antifouling coatings by predicting performance, identifying structure–property relationships, and optimizing formulations while reducing experimental effort. Nevertheless, the direct application of AI and ML specifically to marine antifouling coating design remains relatively limited, and much of the available evidence originates from broader materials science and coating research. Therefore, this review critically examines the emerging application of AI and ML to sustainable polymeric marine antifouling coatings, while distinguishing between directly demonstrated antifouling applications and transferable approaches from related materials systems. The review focuses on the application of AI for predicting fouling resistance, durability, corrosion protection, and environmental sustainability and evaluates the extent to which these approaches can be translated to marine antifouling systems. Key challenges, including data scarcity, heterogeneous experimental datasets, lack of standardized testing protocols, limited field validation, and model interpretability, are highlighted, together with future opportunities in digital twins, explainable AI, generative AI, and autonomous materials discovery for next-generation sustainable antifouling coatings. By critically assessing the current evidence, methodological limitations, and research gaps, this review identifies priorities for developing reliable AI-assisted antifouling coating design frameworks and proposes a staged pathway from standardized data generation and predictive modeling toward experimental validation, active learning, and autonomous materials discovery. AI and machine learning approaches for sustainable marine antifouling coatings are critically reviewed. Current evidence is distinguished between direct antifouling applications and transferable materials-science approaches. Key challenges include data scarcity, heterogeneous datasets, limited standardization, and field validation. Emerging tools include explainable AI, generative AI, digital twins, and autonomous experimentation. A staged roadmap toward predictive, validated, and sustainable antifouling coating design is proposed.

papers.title: Topological analysis of fixed points and horizon phenomena in model predictive control
papers.abstract: Η διπλωματική εργασία διερευνά πώς ο ορίζοντας πρόβλεψης επηρεάζει τη δυναμική κλειστού βρόχου σε συστήματα που ελέγχονται με Οικονομικό Προβλεπτικό Έλεγχο Μοντέλου (EMPC). Το βασικό ερώτημα είναι πότε μια μεταβολή του ορίζοντα οδηγεί σε ποιοτικές αλλαγές —όπως μετατόπιση σταθερών σημείων, αλλαγή ευστάθειας ή συνοριακές συγκρούσεις— και πότε η επίδρασή της γίνεται πρακτικά αμελητέα. Για τη γραμμική περίπτωση χρησιμοποιούνται η πολυπαραμετρική τετραγωνική βελτιστοποίηση και η ανάλυση ενεργού συνόλου. Με αυτά τα εργαλεία μελετώνται οι τμηματικά αφινικοί νόμοι ανάδρασης, τα σταθερά σημεία και οι διασχίσεις των συνόρων κρίσιμων περιοχών. Στη μη γραμμική περίπτωση εξετάζεται η σύγκλιση των ελεγκτών πεπερασμένου ορίζοντα προς τον ελεγκτή άπειρου ορίζοντα. Ένας κατάλληλος μηχανισμός σύγκρισης λύσεων διαφορετικής διάστασης, μαζί με υποθέσεις ισχυρής κανονικότητας και εκθετικής απόσβεσης της ευαισθησίας, οδηγεί σε εκθετική σύγκλιση του νόμου ανάδρασης και της απεικόνισης κλειστού βρόχου σε νόρμα C¹. Τα θεωρητικά αποτελέσματα υποστηρίζονται από έξι αριθμητικά παραδείγματα, γραμμικά και μη γραμμικά. Όσο το ενεργό σύνολο παραμένει αμετάβλητο, οι νόμοι ανάδρασης, οι Ιακωβιανές και τα σταθερά σημεία προσεγγίζουν γρήγορα τη λύση μεγάλου ορίζοντα. Κοντά όμως σε αλλαγές ενεργών περιορισμών, η συνέχεια μπορεί να διατηρείται ενώ η C¹ ομαλότητα χάνεται. Τα αποτελέσματα δείχνουν ότι ο ορίζοντας πρόβλεψης δεν καθορίζει μόνο το υπολογιστικό κόστος· επηρεάζει και την ίδια τη δυναμική του συστήματος. Για αρκετά μεγάλες τιμές, η επίδρασή του φθίνει εκθετικά, υπό τις υποθέσεις της ανάλυσης.

papers.title: SOMA: Stack-of-Objects Manipulation using a Quadruped Robot
papers.abstract: Executing heavy-duty physical manipulation in unpredictable environments remains a major challenge for quadrupedal robots lacking dedicated manipulators. This paper presents SOMA, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for whole-body non-prehensile manipulation of multi-object stacks using a quadruped robot. Unlike traditional methods restricted to two-dimensional planar pushing, SOMA integrates explicit robot base-height control, unlocking full three-dimensional pushing strategies. This capability enables the quadruped to manipulate complex payload stacks as a unified system while preventing relative sliding or tipping of upper layers. The architecture factorizes control into a high-level manipulation policy using a Simplified Structured State Space Sequence (S5) encoder to reason over long-horizon temporal history and predict bounded target tracking commands via Beta distributions, and a low-level locomotion policy that dynamically adapts leg stance configurations. In extensive simulation benchmarks, SOMA achieves a $90.3\%$ success rate for single-object reposing and up to $90.1\%$ for dynamic two-box stacks under stringent error margins ($0.05\text{ m}$ position error, $1^\circ$ orientation error). Finally, we validate zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on a Unitree Go1 quadruped robot across diverse payload masses and geometries, demonstrating active base-height adjustments to maintain traction and balance during heavy pushing tasks.

papers.title: LEAP: Gradient Flow Augmented Lagrangian Trajectory Optimization for Contact Constrained Robots
papers.abstract: Generating dynamically feasible motions for legged and manipulating robots requires solving a large, nonlinear, non-convex optimal control problem (OCP) in which contact wrenches must satisfy friction-cone constraints throughout the motion, not only at isolated instants. Existing solvers are sensitive to the initial guess and scale poorly with the number of joints. This paper introduces LEAP, which transcribes the OCP with pseudospectral collocation and, instead of a Newton or SQP solve, integrates a primal--dual gradient flow of a Powell--Hestenes--Rockafellar augmented Lagrangian to compute a solution. Because the flow is stiff, this paper designs a linearly implicit integrator with a Gauss--Newton metric, momentum, and a merit-based step controller that keeps the augmented Lagrangian monotone. Across locomotion benchmarks on five robot platforms, from planar hoppers to 32-joint humanoids, LEAP is the only method to solve every tested problem, achieves substantial speedups over Crocoddyl and Aligator on several benchmarks, and reaches trackable references at smaller compute budgets. The resulting trajectories are validated by tracking them in a high-fidelity simulator and on hardware. We will make the code public upon final acceptance of this paper.

papers.title: Planning to Learn: Real-Time Robust Adaptive Control on the GPU with Guaranteed Future Learning
papers.abstract: Robust adaptive control is vital for keeping robots safe while actively reducing uncertainty in unfamiliar settings. However, traditional methods are often conservative since they fail to account for guaranteed future parameter learning during planning and struggle to scale to high-dimensional systems. In this work, we present A-SLS, a learning-aware robust adaptive model predictive control (RAMPC) framework based on system-level synthesis. A-SLS forecasts future parameter uncertainty and preserves correlations between process disturbances, parameter error, and estimate updates to construct tight, guaranteed reachable sets that account for future information gain. We also develop a GPU-accelerated A-SLS solver to enable real-time performance. Across nonlinear robotic systems, A-SLS reduces reachable-tube conservativeness, maintains real-time performance, and scales to whole-body control for a quadruped with 61 states, 8 uncertain parameters, and 12 control inputs. We further demonstrate the approach on hardware, where a physical Crazyflie drone learns an uncertain dynamics parameter online to stabilize on the fly.

papers.title: Sign Betting for Misspecified Regression: Variance Adaptivity and Optimal Approximation
papers.abstract: We study bounded regression under model misspecification, evaluating a function $f$ by its $L_1(P_X)$ distance to the conditional mean $η(x)=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X=x]$, rather than the standard $L_2(P_X)$. This $L_1$ metric is natural for downstream decision problems such as bandits and reinforcement learning. We analyze the min--max estimator of Baraud & Maillard (2025), which we call \emph{sign-betting regression}. Our main results show that sign-betting regression achieves high-probability $L_1$ oracle inequalities under misspecification. Under realizability, our bound adapts to the average conditional variance and recovers the variance-adaptive rate of Li et al. (2026). We further characterize the optimal universal approximation factor for proper learning by showing that sign betting achieves factor 3, while no proper learner can satisfy a distribution-free, high-probability $L_1$ oracle inequality with a universal approximation factor strictly below 3. We extend the upper-bound analysis beyond finite classes and complement the theory with experiments in synthetic and real-world model-selection tasks.

papers.title: Pixels to Tokens: Token Space Efficient Active Learning for Low-Budget Semantic Segmentation
papers.abstract: While foundation models and vision transformers (ViTs) have redefined visual representations, current active learning (AL) strategies for these backbones largely operate at the patch or region level, where annotation requirements remain high due to extensive pixel labeling. Extending ViT-based AL to the pixel-level, low-budget regime is uniquely challenging: with as little as one pixel query per image, a method must simultaneously identify the most informative locations and train a reliable decoder head from an extremely sparse signal. We introduce TEAL (Token-space Efficient Active Learning), the first pixel-level AL framework built around ViT representations. TEAL uses a frozen ViT backbone and performs diversity-based selection directly on its native token lattice, avoiding the artifacts introduced by interpolating token embeddings to dense pixel resolutions. Our framework applies a two-level MaxHerding strategy over multi-layer token descriptors to select representative candidates, followed by margin-based uncertainty refinement on a finer decoder grid. Across CamVid, Cityscapes, ADE20K, and Pascal Context, TEAL consistently outperforms previous baselines under extreme label scarcity, improving over the strongest baseline by up to +24.36 mIoU with a single labeled pixel (px) per image, and reaching up to 97% of fully supervised performance with just 10 px. To rigorously establish the source of the gains, we further show that the improvements persist when all baselines are equipped with the same DINOv3 backbone, demonstrating that coupling token-space selection with uncertainty refinement on the decoder grid makes ViT token geometry an effective foundation for extremely low-budget active segmentation.

papers.title: Optimally Trading Energy for Information through Speed Trajectory Optimization of Sustainably Powered Mobile Robots
papers.abstract: Sustainably powered mobile robots enable long-duration observational missions by harvesting energy from the environment. However, effective autonomy requires the robots to make decisions as to how to allocate this energy to maximize information quality over time. In this paper, we study a persistent (infinite-horizon) speed trajectory optimization problem that is posed as a periodic optimal control problem in which a robot repeatedly traverses a fixed closed path, coupling a super-linear propulsion cost with dynamic information gain and decay. Using the information-theoretic quantity of clarity as an information metric, we first derive the necessary conditions for optimal control. We then derive a number of specialized follow-on properties, which characterize (i) the nature of the optimal control when points on the path are of varying importance and when they are of equal importance, along with (ii) a high-speed information limit that is approached when energy reserves approach infinity. We illustrate the information-optimal speed trajectories on a simple example in order to showcase key trends that are followed under the optimized speed profile. This is followed by a simulation study based on the persistent characterization of salinity in the Chesapeake Bay, illustrating the practical merit of applying the results from this work.

papers.title: Time-partitioning Gaussian Process Mixture Model
papers.abstract: We propose the Time-partitioning Gaussian Process Mixture Model (TPGPMM), a Bayesian nonparametric framework for identifying persistent regimes and modelling nonstationary dependence in time series. The model combines an adaptive Pitman--Yor prior on contiguous segmentations with regime-specific Gaussian processes, without imposing Markovian within-regime dependence. Learning the Pitman--Yor discount parameter allows adaptation to homogeneous and heterogeneous regime lengths.   A split--merge Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampler with exact Gibbs boundary updates jointly learns change points and model hyperparameters, quantifying uncertainty over segmentations and within-regime dynamics. With an RBF kernel and a fixed, conservative observation-noise level, TPGPMM favours sparse segmentations that distinguish persistent shifts from transient shocks. Simulations demonstrate recovery of the regime structure. Applications to the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) and the 10-year United States Treasury yield identify regimes aligned with major market and monetary-policy events.   Variants that estimate observation noise improve predictive accuracy relative to the main specification, but can produce less sparse or less event-aligned segmentations. A variant with regime-specific means fits better than a fitted stationary Gaussian process and forecasts about as accurately. These results highlight a trade-off between interpretable regime identification and predictive accuracy.

papers.title: Selection-Safe Conformal Early Exit: Distribution-Free Coverage under Adaptive Depth
papers.abstract: Calibrating a conformal prediction set at each early exit does not preserve coverage once a data-dependent exit is selected. We construct one terminal path score from prefix maxima, calibrate a single split-conformal quantile, and return nested prefix sets that all contain the valid terminal set. The guarantee is selection-safe without an alpha/L correction and holds simultaneously for every post-calibration label-free stopping policy that preserves terminal-set containment. We also bound the efficiency cost of the path maximum by the empirical tail of the early-over-terminal score excess. Across eight encoder task-backbone cells, pathwise selection attains macro coverage 0.901 versus 0.814 for naive layerwise selection, with average set size 1.41 and latency fraction 0.71. On CIFAR-100 with a 24-exit ViT-L/16 (n_cal=500), first-eligible stopping at budget b=4 attains coverage 0.902, set size 2.76, and latency fraction 0.57, and the same calibration supports deployment-time budget changes without refitting. In a joint exit-count/calibration-size sweep at n=100, pathwise set size moves only from 3.02 to 3.11 as exits increase from 4 to 24, while Bonferroni degenerates to the full label space for 12 or more exits. Paired comparison against MinSE valid selection at (n,L)=(100,24) gives a set-size difference of 0.80 [0.47, 1.13]. Full-vocabulary decoder experiments remain a negative boundary, with sets of 7,162-9,620 tokens. Pathwise calibration is most useful when candidate exits are many relative to calibration size, when budgets change after calibration, and when shallow heads return actionable sets.

papers.title: Learning Topology-Aware Representations for Mechanics-Relevant TPMS Metamaterials
papers.abstract: Learning informative representations of mechanical Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) metamaterials is important for mechanics analysis and structural design, yet existing methods have rarely explicitly supervised learned representations with information about global structural connectivity that is relevant to mechanical response. We propose a topology-aware representation learning framework that integrates persistent homology into a DMAE backbone to explicitly encode global structural connectivity. A persistence-guided masking strategy prioritizes patches associated with persistent topological features, while an auxiliary persistent-homology decoder encourages the latent representation to retain information about topological feature counts across connected components, tunnels, and voids. We evaluate the learned representations on two complementary TPMS datasets using family classification, mechanical-property classification, unsupervised clustering, and regression. Across the two datasets, our method demonstrates strong performance in both structural family and mechanical-property classification, improving family classification by up to 3.9% while achieving the best linear-probe performance. More notably, unsupervised property-clustering performance improves by up to 26.7% and 51.5% across the two datasets, while strong regression performance is retained with $R^2=0.993$. These results establish persistent topology as an effective inductive bias for representation learning of complex three-dimensional mechanical metamaterials.

papers.abstract: This research is motivated by the importance of developing students' religious character through Islamic Religious Education amidst various social, family, and digital media challenges. The study aims to analyze the forms and implementation of Islamic Religious Education (IRE) teachers' pedagogical strategies in shaping students' religious character, identify the supporting and inhibiting factors, and analyze their implications for students' religious character development at SMP Laboratorium UM Malang. This study adopted a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, with IRE teachers as the primary data sources, supported by the principal and students. Data analysis followed the Miles and Huberman model, comprising data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification. Data trustworthiness was ensured through source, method, and theoretical triangulation. The results indicate that: (1) The pedagogical strategies of IRE teachers are implemented by integrating classroom learning (active learning, case studies, role-playing, and role modeling) with the institutionalization of school religious culture (habitual congregational prayers, Qur'an memorization/Tahfidz, TABAKU, and the 3S culture: Senyum, Salam, Sapa). (2) Supporting factors include teachers' digital-adaptive pedagogical competence, adequate mosque facilities, a strong religious culture, and harmonious synergy between the school and parents. Inhibiting factors include diverse religious backgrounds and home habituation, negative influences from social/digital media, and students' emotional burnout. (3) Evaluation is conducted internally through regular teacher meetings and externally via the Three-Way Conference forum. The implications of these pedagogical strategies are evidenced by improved worship discipline, enhanced moral conduct and politeness, a declining trend in disciplinary violations, and the formation of habituated religious expressions (kalimat thayyibah) in students' daily lives.

papers.title: Probabilistic modelling of buildings as networks
papers.abstract: Buildings are complex systems whose reliability and robustness depend not only on the components, but also on how they are organised, which dictates how damage propagates across spatial scales. In this paper, we develop a probabilistic building model based on network theory that abstracts redundant compartments as nodes and failure propagation between adjacent compartments as probabilistic edges, such that progressive collapse is represented as a stochastic contagion process equivalent to bond percolation. A percolation-based threshold is introduced to characterise the transition from a local to a systemic failure regime and provide a reference point for sensitivity to failure propagation. To move segmentation beyond qualitative provisions, a risk-equivalence criterion is formulated to determine a risk-neutral calibration point for the failure propagation probability, and an analytical approximation is derived for regular three-dimensional lattices to support early-stage evaluations without extensive numerical analyses. Application examples involving a three-dimensional lattice structure demonstrate how segmentation effectiveness is governed by topology and failure propagation and is approximately independent of the spontaneous compartment failure probability for small spontaneous compartment failure probabilities, implying that improving compartment reliability cannot compensate for insufficient segmentation. The examples further show that increasing continuity and the failure propagation probability can markedly increase the likelihood of progressive and disproportionate collapse, while a high likelihood of progressive collapse is not synonymous with complete system collapse. Overall, the framework provides a basis for defining explicit, topology-dependent performance objectives for segmentation and for supporting reliability-based and risk-informed approaches to mitigating progressive collapse in buildings.

papers.title: Predictive Machine Learning Models for Process Parameters in Additively Manufactured CoCrMo Alloys for Dental Applications
papers.abstract: Dental disease prevalence has increased the demand for effective dental implants. Laser Engineered Net Shaping (LENS) can produce complex geometries through controlled process parameters. Machine learning (ML), on the other hand, enables data driven parametric prediction in Additive Manufacturing (AM), though reliability depends on data quality. This study explores a framework for integration of AM and Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) based data synthesis with ML trained on 108 synthetic samples to enhance parametric prediction and surface quality control. Model validation presented robust performance, with ANN achieving R2 values of 0.981 for surface roughness (governing osseointegration), 0.955 for microhardness (governing wear resistance), and 0.973 for porosity (governing structural integrity), while the best RF prediction performance achieved an R2 of 0.967 for surface roughness, with both models yielding <1.5% prediction error for microhardness. These findings highlight the potential applicability of synthetically generated data to improve scalability and reproducibility of data for ML training in ML based multi-objective optimization of LENS produced CoCrMo alloys for dental applications.

These strategies were manifested through disciplined and courteous behavior modeled by the teachers; the habit of singing the national anthem and respecting national symbols; question-and-answer sessions and simple discussions; the provision of praise and motivation; and linking the material to students’ daily lives. Conversely, inhibiting factors include the influence of digital media, limitations in contextual learning resources, and differences in students’ characteristics and readiness to learn. These findings indicate that fostering nationalism requires strategies that are consistent, concrete, and integrated into both the learning process and the madrasah’s culture.
